title: Add exact-role manifests and deterministic PostgreSQL grant plans
description:
## Outcome

Add a compact application-owned exact-role manifest to `batter-sqlx`. One
validated manifest compiles into the existing low-level `AuthorityPolicy` and a
deterministic, pure plan of role-targeted PostgreSQL `GRANT` statements. The
existing verifier remains the sole ACL evaluator.

## Scope

Implement Milestone 2 and the manifest-specific interfaces in
`.agent/plans/batter-7r3.6-compact-verification-adoption.md`. Add grouped relation
and column declarations, exact existing `RoutineSignature` identities,
required-and-provisioned versus allowed-only purpose, exact PUBLIC delivery,
row-type PUBLIC-USAGE and SECURITY DEFINER options, checked expansion/capacity,
normalization, conflict rejection, and deterministic quoting/rendering.

Keep construction pure and application-neutral. Add no database connection,
provisioner, SQL parser, serde format, proc macro, or second policy evaluator.
Preserve the existing low-level function signatures and policy-struct layouts.

## Acceptance

- Grouping and input order compile to one normalized policy and grant plan;
  exact duplicates are idempotent and conflicting declarations fail.
- Required, allowed-only, PUBLIC delivery, ownership, grant-option ceilings,
  row-type usage, and definer allowance retain their independent semantics.
- Exact PUBLIC denial overrides permissive defaults; allowed-only declarations
  and defaults emit no SQL.
- Invalid identifiers, type identities, privilege/object pairs, contradictions,
  and over-capacity input fail before I/O or partial output.
- Rendering is deterministic and identifier-safe, uses `ON ROUTINE`, accepts
  explicit database context only when a database grant exists, and cannot emit
  role creation, revocation, credentials, transactions, or execute SQL.
- A generic example constructs policy through the manifest; the existing
  low-level construction path still compiles.
- Focused format, unit, Clippy, rustdoc, and applicable Jig checks pass. This task
  does not claim live protected-executor or pinned-consumer completion.
acceptance_criteria: The compact manifest compiles to the existing low-level authority policy and a deterministic pure grant plan; offline equivalence, conflict, capacity, PUBLIC, option, identifier, and rendering tests pass without a second evaluator or database I/O.

Comprehensive all-reviewer repair and final closure passes converged; low residual coverage is tracked in batter-h2r. Both supported toolchain matrices, ten HTTP smokes, focused SQLx tests/doctests, and all final Jig gates passed. Live grant execution remains explicitly deferred to batter-r2a.

comments.author: aa
comments.text: ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment (review loop round 4): independent Codex and Claude reviewers confirmed that a declared relation row-type PUBLIC choice was not pinned against permissive type discovery defaults. Earlier rounds separately found implicit column-parent policy and a column PUBLIC deny that could not subtract the same parent-relation PUBLIC grant. These are one recurring exact-PUBLIC translation invariant across relation, column, and composite row-type objects. Source evidence: manifest/compile.rs emits only the declared GrantTarget override; authority/discovery.rs later expands type PUBLIC defaults; authority/requests.rs consults allow_row_type_public_usage for row types. Failure scenario: schema/user-schema discovery plus defaults.types PUBLIC USAGE can make a default-deny relation pass while its row type remains PUBLIC-readable. Classification: implementation mistake in the new high-level compiler, not a foundation/adapter ownership gap. The established AuthorityPolicy already represents exact PublicObject::Type overrides; callers should not reconstruct this link. Bounded in-scope remedy: compile one exact row-type type override per relation (empty for deny, USAGE for allow), charge it in generated-policy capacity, and prove expanded-verifier tests. This removes the cause rather than adding caller instructions. No separate design Bead is needed unless the remedy exposes a low-level policy limitation.

comments.text: Comprehensive low-severity all-reviewer loop closure: after four repair rounds and the user-directed fresh follow-up pass, Claude and Codex reported no actionable findings. The current relation-name PublicObject::Type override therefore matches the verifier's typrelid-selected row type. Remaining low test/evidence gaps are tracked in batter-h2r; live render/apply/verifier proof remains with batter-r2a as already scoped. title: Replace duplicated downstream browser transport with Batter
description:
## Outcome

Cut one existing Axum application over to the browser credential transport delivered by the owning Batter feature, advance every coordinated Batter dependency to the same exact available revision, and delete the superseded local browser-boundary implementation.

## Code scope

- Replace local configured-origin parsing/canonicalization with `BrowserOrigin` while retaining application link construction and environment schema.
- Replace local exact-Origin, Fetch Metadata, and JSON mutation checks with one configured `MutationPolicy` reused by the actual mutation routes.
- Replace local named-cookie scanning and set/removal formatting with `read_cookie` and `BrowserCookie` while retaining the application secret-token type and credential-error mapping.
- Replace local private-response middleware with Batter's adapter middleware.
- Compare the downstream Referrer-Policy before cutover. Batter emits `same-origin` so same-origin HTML form mutations retain Origin while cross-origin referrers are withheld; record and deliberately resolve any existing policy difference.
- Remove the local surface trait and helper functions that Batter supersedes; do not leave forwarding wrappers as deferred cleanup.
- Preserve application-owned auth/session storage, invitations, rate limits, direct-peer identity, JSON extractor mapping, error envelope, retry advice, routing, and server-side revocation.

## Provenance and limits

Record exact old/new Batter pins, removed mechanisms, preserved contracts, and executed downstream evidence in the consumer's existing adoption record. Treat availability at a concrete source revision as a prerequisite; a closed tracker item or uncommitted Batter work is insufficient. Report generic adoption friction on the owning Batter feature after checking current source and open/closed Beads. Do not create provider sessions, infrastructure, commits, pushes, publication, or deployment without their separate authorization.
acceptance_criteria: One real downstream application uses one coordinated Batter revision containing the browser feature. Its local origin parser, cookie scan/serialization/removal, mutation-signal checks, private-response middleware, and surface trait are removed rather than wrapped. Secure and explicit loopback behavior, cookie names/attributes/lifetime, duplicate and malformed credential handling, exact Origin/Fetch-Site/JSON rejection precedence, the deliberate `same-origin` Referrer-Policy decision, private headers, public/admin routing, and application error envelopes remain behaviorally covered. Token meaning, sessions/accounts, authorization, rate limiting, trusted peer identity, invitations, and revocation remain application-owned. The consumer records exact old/new pins and adoption friction, and all repository-required Rust, HTTP, contract, SQLx, and structured gates applicable to the changed paths pass. This is an actual code cutover, not an adoption-certification or evidence-only exercise.
notes: Adoption precondition from the feature review: marker-protected routes require a potentially trustworthy mutation URL and supported clients that emit Sec-Fetch-Site. The fixed Referrer-Policy: same-origin preserves a non-CORS form Origin only when the page and mutation target share one origin; inspect any cross-origin form layout before cutover.

title: Implement composable browser credential transport in batter-axum
description:
## Outcome

Add `batter_axum::browser`, a public Axum adapter boundary for browser-carried opaque credentials. Applications can validate trusted browser origins, read one named cookie without duplicate ambiguity, append and remove host-only cookies, validate configured mutation signals, and apply private-response headers without adopting a Batter account, session, authorization, or wire-error model.

The implementation is specified by `.agent/plans/browser-credential-transport.md`.

## Runtime scope

- Add validated HTTPS and explicit loopback-HTTP origin values backed internally by the current `url` crate.
- Add validated cookie name/value, SameSite, visibility, lifetime, strict/target-only input parsing, and host-only `Path=/` set/removal behavior backed internally by the current `cookie` crate where it preserves Batter's stricter contract.
- Scan every Cookie field, reject duplicate target cookies, never decode opaque values, append rather than replace independent Set-Cookie fields, reject an existing same-name response field before mutation, require `__Host-` plus Secure for HTTPS, and reject invalid secure/development combinations before serving.
- Add a non-empty mutation policy requiring exact configured Origin or an exact custom marker. Origin-only policies may optionally select `RejectCrossSite` or `RequireSameOrigin`; every policy containing a marker automatically requires `RequireSameOrigin` and cannot weaken or duplicate that Fetch Metadata guard. Optionally enforce the exact `application/json` media type.
- Add typed sanitized construction/request failures with deterministic Origin, Fetch Metadata, marker, then content-type precedence. Do not include observed or expected credential/header values in errors or telemetry.
- Add pure and middleware forms of the fixed private-response policy: `Cache-Control: no-store`, `Referrer-Policy: same-origin`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`.

## Ownership limits

Keep token generation/parsing, signed or session-bound CSRF protocols, CORS, bearer precedence, account/session persistence, authentication, authorization, route selection, response envelopes, and server-side revocation application-owned. Do not add Domain/path customization, a cookie jar, signed/encrypted cookies, a security-policy DSL, a new runtime task, or a foundation dependency on HTTP.

## Delivery shape

Implement the source, public rustdoc, failure-path/public integration coverage, dependency/lock changes, and current architecture/guarantee/status/testing/reference/changelog/guide updates in this feature. Tests, review, documentation, and evidence are acceptance obligations, not separate Beads. The feature is not blocked by facade extraction; if the facade lands first, use its actual re-export path without duplicating types. No commit, push, publication, or deployment is authorized by this record.
design:
Recurring marker-policy assessment, 2026-09-15.

Evidence: review repair 1 rejected Fetch-safelisted and forbidden request names; repair 2 rejected values whose surrounding whitespace Fetch normalizes. The terminal fifth-round review demonstrated a third manifestation: Upgrade-Insecure-Requests is neither safelisted nor forbidden but a browser can attach it to a cross-site form without script or CORS preflight. A marker-only policy can therefore accept a cross-site request when Fetch Metadata is absent.

Classification: adapter structural deficiency. RequiredHeader accepts arbitrary HTTP names while its public contract implies browser provenance that no finite browser-header denylist can enforce. Adding more browser-generated names would cover only another case. Documentation-only narrowing would leave the cross-site invariant as a caller obligation.

Alternatives: (1) extend the denylist—rejected as open-ended symptom repair; (2) document marker-name selection as caller-owned—rejected because marker-only remains a valid but fragile protected path; (3) pair every required-header policy with adapter-owned strict Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin—selected. This matches the demonstrated marker consumer, fails closed when Fetch Metadata is absent, and makes any browser-attached marker insufficient by itself. Exact-Origin policies remain separately selectable. Non-browser clients can still forge browser signals; CORS and application authentication remain outside this boundary.

Authorized remedy: hard-cut over MutationPolicy::required_header so it installs RequireSameOrigin and cannot be weakened or duplicated. Update rustdoc, examples, tests, contracts, validation, and tracker scope. Then restart the complete low-threshold review-fix loop as directed by the user-supplied workflow.
acceptance_criteria: `batter_axum::browser` exposes no `cookie`/`url` implementation types or application domain types; its Axum/http transport types remain adapter-native, and the Tokio foundation remains HTTP-free. HTTPS/loopback origin construction, strict cookie-name/value validation, all-field duplicate-aware cookie reads, host-only root-path set/removal, independent-name Set-Cookie append and same-name response rejection, explicit SameSite/HttpOnly/lifetime choices, secure `__Host-` enforcement, and sanitized errors satisfy the plan matrices. Mutation policy cannot be empty; all configured exact-Origin/custom-marker/Fetch-Site/JSON checks use exact multiplicity and deterministic typed rejection, every marker policy automatically requires exact same-origin Fetch Metadata, and no policy claims authentication or complete CSRF protection. Private-response behavior covers inner success, application rejection, and fallback without altering status/body/extensions or duplicating HTTP observations. Current `cookie`/`url` contracts and MSRVs are recorded; public rustdoc and focused failure-path tests pass; complete batter-axum, both supported-toolchain verification matrices, required HTTP smokes, and applicable Jig gates pass with honest platform limits. Contracts, status, references, changelog, and owning guides match the implemented boundary. No process-only follow-up is required for feature completion.
close_reason: Implemented the batter-axum browser credential transport boundary with validated origins, duplicate-aware opaque cookie reads, fixed host-only set/removal, strict mutation policies, sanitized rejections, and private-response middleware. The 33-case public target, 23 positive plus five compile-fail doctests, strict Clippy, both Rust 1.98.1 and 1.94.0 verification matrices, all ten HTTP smoke profiles, and applicable Jig gates passed. The restarted low-threshold Claude/Codex/Cursor loop converged with no actionable findings; its chronology-only closure obligation was verified by all three reviewers. Downstream adoption remains open; no push, publication, or deployment was performed.

title: Separate HTTP observation from request admission and deadlines
description:
## Problem and reproduced evidence

HTTP observation currently shares the request admission/deadline boundary. In crates/batter-axum/src/lib.rs, request_scope_inner constructs the private HttpObservation before the readiness gate. Consequently, gate rejections are already observed, but probes and fallback mounted outside request_scope are not. A downstream consumer removed its outer TraceLayer during adoption and lost those HTTP completion events. The Batter HTTP example also merges probes after applying request_scope, so the coverage problem is reproducible from the recommended composition.

| Scenario | Response status | HTTP completion events |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Application success | 200 | 1 |
| Liveness probe | 200 | 0 |
| Readiness failure | 503 | 0 |
| Unmatched fallback | 404 | 0 |
| Method rejection on an application route | 405 | 1 |
| Drain rejection | 503 | 1 |

On Rust 1.98.1, all 16 Batter adapter tests and all six downstream HTTP tests passed. Their passing results do not establish coverage of this composition: tests/telemetry.rs exercises fallback by installing the combined request_scope across its router. Existing tests/scoped_dispatch.rs proves aborted combined middleware retains the original subscriber and nested span destruction, but does not exercise independent observation.

The disposable reproduction remains at /tmp/batter-http-investigation-zpp1c_u_/src/main.rs on the investigating machine. This is transient supporting evidence, not a required future test fixture; the matrix and assembly instructions here suffice to recreate it using generic routes.

## Delivery scope

Add independent HTTP observation middleware to batter-axum, with no lifecycle handle or deadline policy requirement. Keep HttpObservation private. Add an admission/deadline entry point that retains RequestPolicy, readiness admission, native OperationContext insertion, forced cancellation, and configured failure rendering. Preserve request_scope as a compatibility wrapper over the shared observation and admission implementations. RequestPolicy continues to combine readiness and deadlines; this task separates observation from that combined policy.

Update the HTTP example and adoption guidance to assemble guarded application routes using the admission-only entry point, merge unguarded probes and fallback, apply observation to the assembled router, and apply trusted server request identity outermost. The outer observer must surround middleware that rejects or transforms responses within the intended observed boundary. Migration must replace the inner combined request_scope when adding outer observation, so the supported composition emits one HTTP completion per request. Explicitly document the behavior of nesting the observer with the legacy combined wrapper; do not accidentally promise deduplication.

Preserve first-poll dispatcher capture using batter::telemetry::with_current_dispatch. Observation guards, instrumented futures and their nested spans must all remain inside its protected future through polling and full destruction. Preserve method normalization, matched route templates or <unmatched>, actual response status, outcome and latency, without logging raw paths, query values, headers, bodies, error contents or untrusted methods. Trusted request correlation remains application-owned.

## Axum composition constraint

Axum 0.8.9 Router::layer runs after routing and only covers routes/fallback assembled before the layer is applied. A route appended afterward bypasses it. A literal Tower wrapper outside routing sees no MatchedPath when the current observer creates its span, even for a matched route. Both behaviors were executed in the reproduction. Use the assembled-router placement to preserve sanitized route templates; test new routes added through that normal assembly path and state the late-route limitation. Do not describe the conceptual ordering diagram as literal pre-routing middleware unless route metadata capture is redesigned and tested.

Primary reference: https://docs.rs/crate/axum/0.8.9/source/src/docs/routing/layer.md ; also inspect the resolved axum source and record version-specific semantics in docs/references.md at implementation time.

Owning package: batter-axum. Parent: batter-faj, observability across ownership boundaries. This work is independently actionable; it does not wait for database reference work, exporters, request metadata extraction, or the separate upstream admission integration in batter-97p. Related work is context, not a blocking dependency.

The observed lifetime ends at response construction. A dropped, polled response future may emit dropped without a response status; dropping a body after response construction is a different lifetime. Do not imply body streaming, WebSocket ownership, universal disconnect propagation, panic recovery, runtime-death finalization, or exactly-once log delivery. Library global subscribers and panic hooks remain forbidden.

title: Parse provider retry delays without shortening their lower bound
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Wire delay formats need explicit clock and overflow handling before entering the core monotonic retry budget.

## Scope

Add a small outbound-provider example with an example-owned Retry-After parser and concrete parse errors; HTTP parsing and date-parser dependencies remain outside the foundation's public/normal dependency API. Declare the new target explicitly in `crates/batter/Cargo.toml` because `autoexamples = false`; enable its tests with `test = true` and document `cargo test -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked` plus `cargo run -p batter --example provider_retry_after --locked`. Verify the applicable primary Retry-After/HTTP-date protocol sections and selected date-parser version before implementing, and record them in docs/references.md. The parser accepts one header-field value: nonnegative ASCII decimal seconds or the HTTP-date forms required by that protocol. Use injected SystemTime for date conversion and return a nonnegative Duration; a past/current date or zero seconds is a valid zero floor. Malformed or unrepresentable input is a concrete parse failure; the example stops rather than silently turning an unreadable provider instruction into an immediate retry. Convert the valid floor once at the response/classification boundary; subsequent scheduling uses the unchanged monotonic OperationContext. Missing headers add no provider floor. Parsing never decides replay safety or failure eligibility.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Deterministic parser tests cover zero/positive/leading-zero seconds, required date forms, injected clock before/equal/after the date, allowed surrounding header whitespace, malformed dates, signed/fractional seconds, multiple-field/list input outside the single-value contract, and numeric/date overflow. Do not read the system clock inside parser tests or re-read it during retry sleep.
- Keep valid large delays distinct from unrepresentable values: a representable provider floor beyond remaining execution time reaches RetryDecision::RetryAfter and returns StopReason::InsufficientBudget with the last application E while the total context is still live; malformed/overflow input produces the example's concrete parse failure and stops without inventing a short floor.
- Composition uses `max(existing_backoff_or_jitter, provider_floor)` after jitter/capping. A provider floor can exceed the local backoff cap. Zero/past-date floors still use the policy's positive backoff, and no checked conversion wraps or generates a retry spin.
- ReplaySafety::Never and classifier Stop remain terminal regardless of a valid header. Timeout/cancellation are not classified into retries, and parser diagnostics neither authorize replay nor replace the last application failure with a fabricated elapsed deadline.
- The explicit example test command actually executes parser tests under both supported Rust toolchains; normal workspace verification compiles/runs the declared target as configured. No live external provider is required for this parser/composition example.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- crates/batter/examples/
- crates/batter-core/tests/retry.rs
- docs/references.md

## Dependencies and consumers

title: Bound non-yielding lifecycle tests with a subprocess watchdog
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A cooperative Tokio timer cannot interrupt work that never yields; testing inside the main runtime can hang the entire runner.

## Scope

Add a killable child-process fixture exercising runtime-thread blocking/non-yielding tasks during cancellation and shutdown. Parent uses a wall-clock watchdog, captures completion evidence, kills and reaps the child on timeout, and distinguishes expected non-preemption from a harness hang.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Exercise at least one non-yielding direct task and cooperative control with bounded process duration.
- Assert observable shutdown/report limitations without pretending the child joined or its dependencies were clean.
- A deliberately stuck child cannot hang the test runner; cleanup removes subprocess resources on failure.
- Preserve Linux/macOS scope while explicitly excluding Windows and planned Windows support; remove repository-owned Windows implementations, non-Unix signal fallbacks and Windows CI targets.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- crates/batter/tests/
- crates/batter/src/lifecycle/driver.rs

Work from the repository root. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide before editing. Native Rust/Tokio remains the foundation; Axum is a separate adapter, SQLx remains native application composition, and generic test support stays a leaf. Do not install library global subscribers or panic hooks, recreate upstream queue/provisioning/storage engines, or infer publication/deployment permission.

Use a task-local ExecPlan under .agent/PLANS.md for sufficiently complex implementation. Its steps/evidence belong to this bead; it must not become a second backlog. title: Add protected SQLx ledger schema and ownership verification requests
description:
## Outcome

Add protected high-level verification requests that let a consumer remove
generic SQLx-ledger shape, SECURITY DEFINER configuration, and coarse reachable
ownership catalog queries without merging schema verification into serving-role
authority.

## Scope

Implement Milestone 3 and the safeguard interfaces in
`.agent/plans/batter-7r3.6-compact-verification-adoption.md` only after the
independently owned `batter-7r3.5 -> batter-7r3.12` review prerequisite settles.
Reuse the existing owned verifier executor, caller `OperationContext`, lease,
captured snapshot, relation locking, capacity, rollback, and disposition.

Add exact and installed-subset SQLx 0.9 ledger manifests; a schema-only
configuration request that works under owner or restricted credentials; and an
authority safeguard denying current-database ownership reachable from the
authenticated login. Do not add fields to exhaustively constructible low-level
policy structs or a second executor.

## Acceptance

- New entrypoints accept `&OperationContext` and return the existing
  `OperationError<VerificationError>` boundary; already-cancelled, occupied-pool,
  blocked-inspection, rollback, and retirement behavior remains intact.
- SQLx shape is the six canonical non-dropped, non-null columns plus exact
  `version` primary key. Exact and non-prefix installed-subset history preserve
  checksum/success semantics; late attachment, RLS, inheritance, and overflow
  cannot pass.
- Schema inspection requires exactly the canonical `search_path` setting for all
  scoped definers including trigger/ungranted routines, accepts unrelated GUCs,
  bounds rows and retained bytes, and stays independent from role authority.
- Ownership inspection uses login-rooted INHERIT/SET/ADMIN reachability, includes
  current database and ownership dependencies, distinguishes non-ownership rows,
  retains `objsubid`, and fails incomplete on uninterpretable or over-capacity
  evidence.
- New live tests are explicitly registered in Cargo and the exact live-runner
  inventory. Deterministic concurrency and guard-removal controls reject the
  intended defects on PostgreSQL 18.
- Docs accurately distinguish supported checks, unsupported semantics,
  intentional tightenings, and application-owned policy/provisioning.
acceptance_criteria: Protected requests reuse the caller OperationContext and existing executor; SQLx shape/subset, schema search-path, and reachable ownership contracts pass bounded deterministic PostgreSQL 18 tests and preserve separate schema and role boundaries.
close_reason: Implemented protected SQLx ledger, schema, and ownership verification with reviewed and executable evidence

comments.author: aa
comments.text: ADR-010 assessment after comprehensive pass f560a8f7187be73bf2d4f356686380f8833ec668618e4fe7aa85ee46aaf1f539: Claude and Codex reported the post-proof ledger identity failure as medium; Cursor reported it as high. The earlier repair closed an absent/pre-snapshot name-replacement window by checking pg_locks against the snapshot-visible relation OID, but LedgerLock then discards that OID and both protected and legacy history readers later resolve the qualified name again. A schema rename is compatible with the held relation lock, so the scan can target an unlocked replacement after the proof. This is confirmed recurring invariant evidence, not the unexecuted live suite or a caller mistake. The public protected API asks the adapter to own locking/snapshot/rollback and imposes no coordination obligation on the consumer; the cause is therefore an adapter shared-implementation/design gap. Another timing check would cover only one more window. The bounded in-scope remedy is to replace the boolean Ready state with an identity-bearing protected-ledger value and make metadata, shape and history operate through that retained identity without later name resolution; legacy behavior must remain explicit rather than inherit a false guarantee. A deterministic post-proof replacement control must fail the old mechanism and pass the redesign. This stays within batter-g19 acceptance and does not change application policy. No separate design Bead is needed unless PostgreSQL/SQLx evidence shows the adapter cannot hold an identity-bound scan with its current dependency surface. Live PostgreSQL execution remains unavailable because all three required URLs are absent.

comments.author: aa
comments.text: ADR-010 reassessment after comprehensive pass f978ec53bc5243ba86eed354b0cab7b7fee3aa1a9501895c3c536f0a8cbc0a3a: Codex rated the generated cursor literal defect high; Claude independently found the same root cause at low and a remaining double-name-resolution race at medium. The retained-OID redesign removed late name lookup from metadata and FETCH, but DECLARE still embeds the qualified policy name both as an SQL literal and as a RangeVar. Under standard_conforming_strings=off, accepted backslash-plus-apostrophe identifiers can change parsing. Separately, stale regclass resolution can attest the locked OID while FROM binds an empty replacement. These are shared adapter implementation/design failures, not caller coordination mistakes. The root cause is asking independently parsed name expressions to prove the identity of a server-bound relation. This repair will remove policy text from SQL literals by using only fixed-safe constants, retain the server portal, and attest relation locks acquired while DECLARE binds its RangeVar so an empty replacement cannot pass. It will also close catalog type-namespace, UTF-8 byte-bound, and deterministic barrier gaps. No public caller obligation or application policy change is authorized. Live PostgreSQL remains unavailable, so claims remain limited to compile/list evidence unless URLs become available.

comments.author: aa
comments.text: ADR-010 assessment after terminal comprehensive pass 29637f231630fcfa89108f4a160be80076f2f07f9638ebff4cb22e74af07deac: Cursor rated a supposed explicit pg_database_owner membership path high. PostgreSQL 18 primary documentation states that pg_database_owner always has exactly one implicit member, the current database owner, and that membership both into and out of this predefined role cannot be granted. The reported production path therefore cannot be created through supported PostgreSQL 18 semantics, and the current exception was intended to model that invariant. The review still exposed that the code represents the implicit edge by role name while accepting impossible pg_auth_members rows as ordinary graph evidence. The root repair is to separate the implicit database-owner edge from stored membership evidence and mark any stored edge involving pg_database_owner incomplete as an uninterpretable catalog state. This preserves the real owner finding, refuses malformed evidence, and avoids inventing a grant-based contract PostgreSQL forbids. Claude also confirmed a stale live barrier assertion after query reordering and a legacy type-namespace diagnostic mismatch; those will be repaired at their sources. The live PostgreSQL 18 suite remains unexecuted because all required URLs are absent, so no live outcome is claimed.

The cursor uses a bounded generated name proven absent from pg_cursors and retains its suffix through FETCH; replacement permission and type-resolution failures map to unavailable, the test pause cannot poison its mutex, and InstalledSubset wording is snapshot-specific. The missing PostgreSQL URLs still prevent live execution, and docs/status now says both the rewritten legacy cursor path and protected additions lack current live evidence. title: Stabilize protected ledger index evidence across concurrent DDL
description: Terminal low-severity batter-g19 review finding. Index OIDs are captured from the repeatable-read snapshot while cursor-planning lock evidence observes current relation locks. A concurrently committed replacement index can therefore appear as an unexpected acquired lock and make a conforming protected ledger conservatively incomplete.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic PostgreSQL 18 concurrency control reproduces the false-incomplete window, and the verifier binds or classifies protected index evidence consistently without weakening heap identity, replacement, inheritance, RLS, or fail-closed guarantees.

title: Enforce provider lease and durable retry eligibility boundaries
description: ADR-010 recurring-defect assessment: begin_live_effect hides SQL but evaluates expiry before its FOR UPDATE wait, contradicting the promised post-lock validation. The existing revocation test updates the row and misses lock-only expiry. Separately, record_undispatched cannot accept retry timing; the worker commits retryable effect state before returning native scheduling, so interruption loses the lower bound. These are a private-boundary implementation error plus application protocol persistence gap, not evidence that Batter should become a queue or provider framework. Repair the private lease transaction and atomic provider outcome/eligibility boundary, check eligibility at dispatch authorization, preserve timing on known returned storage failures, and test lock-only expiry and interrupted completion. Evaluate locks acquired later in the transaction too. Pinned Runledger retry delay zero preserves policy backoff; its work reserve is headroom, not a SQL sub-timeout. No backfill/mixed-version obligation. Live reproductions and new consumer evaluation are not yet executed.
acceptance_criteria: Post-lock lease identity/expiry validation cannot be bypassed through any effect mutation. Provider retry not-before is durable with its outcome and gates all replay/dispatch routes. Known timing survives returned storage failures; unpersisted-response process-death limits remain explicit. Focused failure tests, two toolchains, HTTP smokes, exact live suites, contracts/status/validation and Jig evidence updated. No publication, commit, second queue or upstream ownership inversion.
close_reason: Implemented lease post-lock/pre-commit authority and atomic durable provider retry eligibility with protected dispatch checks. title: Borrow composite at-rest ciphertext during canonical decode
description:
## Outcome
A caller holding one canonical encoded sealed payload can decode its structure and open it without a second ciphertext-sized decode buffer. Owned decoding and borrowed split-storage use remain supported. This is a memory-efficiency improvement, not an observed outage or a measured speed/peak-memory claim.

## Evidence and readiness audit
Audited 2026-09-23 at f5e0074e30558599ff65a54f307c75abafc16a2e. `crates/batter-at-rest/src/format.rs::SealedPayload::decode` checks the complete composite, including trailing data, then copies `ciphertext.to_vec()`. `SealedPayloadRef` is Copy and borrows both an existing `Envelope` and a body; it cannot own an envelope parsed during composite decoding. `src/crypto.rs::Keyring::open` already accepts that view, and `decrypt_bytes` allocates the authenticated plaintext buffer. The 64 MiB plaintext limit is a format ceiling, not an endpoint recommendation. `KeyId` owns a String, so owning a decoded header does not imply zero allocations.

## Design and compatibility decision
- Add public `BorrowedSealedPayload<'a>` with private fields: an owned `Envelope` and ciphertext `&'a [u8]`. Provide `decode(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Result<Self, Error>`, `envelope(&self) -> &Envelope`, `ciphertext(&self) -> &[u8]`, and `as_ref(&self) -> SealedPayloadRef<'_>`. Re-export it from `src/lib.rs`; the facade's existing wildcard re-export preserves the same type. Naming is fixed here to make the implementation entry point concrete.
- Canonical flow: `let decoded = BorrowedSealedPayload::decode(&encoded)?; let plaintext = keyring.open(&context, decoded.as_ref())?;`. The encoded buffer outlives the borrowed payload; the returned decrypt view borrows the payload's owned header as well. Do not introduce self-references, leaked allocations, unsafe code, mutable fields, or an authenticated-state claim.
- Preserve existing `SealedPayload::decode`, `SealedPayloadRef::new`, their signatures, the view's Copy behavior, and `Keyring::open`. Use one structural composite parser: owned decode reuses the borrowed parser and copies the body only after the complete parse succeeds, including `Decoder::finish`. A private helper is fine; no second parser or public conversion API is needed.
- Preserve the exact accepted canonical v1 bytes, validation order and public error categories. Decode requires no keys/context and authenticates nothing. Tampering that leaves framing valid is accepted structurally and rejected by open. No mutation of input and no transient ciphertext-sized buffer in borrowed parsing; small header allocations and open's plaintext allocation remain allowed and documented.
- No new format, dependencies, storage/serde/async integration, in-place or streaming decryption, benchmark subsystem, or package-version change. No migration is needed; callers can continue using owned decode or switch back without changing stored values.

## Implementation surfaces
Update `src/format.rs`, `src/lib.rs`, `src/format/tests.rs`, relevant crypto tests, and `tests/public_api.rs` under `crates/batter-at-rest`. Add redacted Debug consistent with existing payload types and rustdoc including a runnable decode/open example. Update the crate README's buffer guidance and ownership/authentication distinction, the implemented row in root `docs/status.md`, and relevant `docs/testing.md` evidence. Extend `scripts/check_facade_features.py` consumer coverage for the new export/type identity. The standalone gate currently copies only `tests/public_api.rs` to its artifact-only consumer. If the public test includes `tests/fixtures/envelope-v1.txt`, extend `scripts/check-batter-at-rest-portability.sh` to copy that fixture into the consumer too; keep any other test support self-contained or copy it explicitly.

## Falsifiable acceptance
1. Public API tests decode an independently generated v1 fixture and a normal seal output through both APIs and open the expected plaintext. Assert the borrowed ciphertext pointer and length equal the exact body subslice of the still-live original encoding (including tag), not merely another view of decoded data. Check the parsing implementation creates no transient body copy; pointer identity alone does not prove allocation counts. No quantitative memory/speed claims without a separate measurement.
2. Use expected-error assertions for bad magic, every truncation, unknown descriptor version, invalid key IDs, inconsistent nested/fixed lengths, header/body oversize, body shorter than `TAG_BYTES`, and trailing data, then check parity between owned and borrowed decoding. Retain the bounded single-byte mutation corpus and canonical round-trip property; parity alone is not an independent oracle when both APIs share the parser. Cover valid empty plaintext (`TAG_BYTES` body), maximum legal body length and maximum key ID; use small headers for declared-oversize rejection where possible.
3. A changed body/tag with valid framing still decodes, then fails open with `AuthenticationFailed`; wrong context and unavailable key keep their existing open errors. The decoded type's names/docs must not imply authentication.
4. Compile-fail lifetime examples attempt to retain the borrowed payload after dropping its encoded backing buffer and to retain its `SealedPayloadRef` after dropping the decoded header owner. Include compiling scoped counterparts so unrelated missing imports cannot satisfy the negative cases. Rustdoc and public consumer checks run at the Rust 1.94 minimum.
5. Existing owned/split APIs, redaction, format vectors and limits remain intact. Exercise direct and facade imports. Do not expose mutable accessors or bypass structural validation on the canonical decoder.

## Verification and delivery
During implementation use Jig work tracking. Run `cargo test -p batter-at-rest --locked`, `cargo clippy -p batter-at-rest --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `node crates/batter-at-rest/tests/fixtures/generate-envelope-v1.mjs --check`, and `scripts/check-batter-at-rest-portability.sh` (exact Rust 1.94 detached/package/unpacked/external consumer). Complete both `bash scripts/verify.sh` and `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh`, rebuilt HTTP smoke profiles from `docs/testing.md#http-process-smoke-test`, and final fresh Jig `api:test` evidence plus required policy gates; reuse eligible receipts rather than repeat passing work. Keep `.jig.toml` and `.agent/jig-contract.json` exhaustive scopes aligned if new inputs require it. Record actual platform/toolchain results and the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment here; proposed checks and fresh-agent evaluations remain unexecuted until recorded. Keep Cargo.lock Cargo-generated. Publication/commits are outside this task's authorization.

Depends on: none. batter-t2uq is an independent metadata-rotation improvement. Either task can ship first; serialize edits/integration of shared format, docs and public-consumer files. If rotation is demonstrated after both land, use its preferred envelope-returning API without making it a prerequisite for borrowed decoding.
acceptance_criteria: Public BorrowedSealedPayload owns only the decoded header and borrows the exact ciphertext subslice of a canonical composite. Its as_ref view opens through unchanged Keyring::open, and owned decode shares structural parsing while preserving all existing signatures, v1 bytes, error categories and trailing-before-copy behavior. Independent fixture/expected-error tests, pointer identity, lifetime compile-fail examples, tampered-body authentication and direct/facade external consumers verify the contract. No unmeasured allocation-free or performance claim is made. Required two-toolchain, HTTP, detached Rust 1.94 package/consumer and fresh Jig verification is recorded before closure.

description:
## Outcome and rationale

Speculative caches, batching, construction graphs and adapter wrappers increase API surface before shared semantics are known.

## Scope

Deferred until two actual application composition roots demonstrate the same need. Collect their partial-startup/shutdown failure behavior, external version contracts and repeated code; record an ADR choosing local duplication, a narrow shared core, or no extraction. Candidate caches/batching/deduplication, bounded queues, construction graphs and service replacement are possibilities, not authorized features. Apply the same evidence threshold to stable integration adapters; circuits/fallback require a measured dependency need.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two consumers and their shared failure semantics are identified with source evidence.
- An ADR explains the smallest justified reuse or explicitly retains separate implementations; no generic DI/cache/runtime is created speculatively.
- Any resulting implementation scope becomes a concrete follow-up delivery bead rather than an unconditional framework backlog.
- The decision distinguishes demonstrated experimental delivery under batter-7r3 from stable/public adapter promotion and speculative frameworks; it neither blocks the concrete extraction track nor counts two examples as two actual application adopters.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

Keep this task deferred for speculative abstractions and stable adapter promotion. batter-7r3 separately authorizes focused experimental operational extraction backed by inspected downstream failure mechanisms and duplicated code: health, SQLx connection disposition, startup, Axum defaults and PostgreSQL verification. This deferred task must not block those concrete delivery tasks or be used to recreate them here. Their acceptance still requires actual consumer adoption evidence, and packages remain unpublished. The two-actual-consumer threshold still applies to stable adapter promotion and broader speculative caches/batching/construction frameworks; examples are not independently deployed adopters, and publication remains a separate decision.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- docs/architecture.md
- docs/adr/
- docs/integrations.md

## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-fms — Prove atomicity, idempotency and durable lifetime with real PostgreSQL

Unblocks: This is a terminal delivery/decision outcome; no artificial consumer is required.

## Verification and governing constraints

Work from the repository root. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide before editing. Native Rust/Tokio remains the foundation; Axum is a separate adapter, SQLx remains native application composition, and generic test support stays a leaf. Preserve downward cancellation, parent deadline clamping, inert factories, explicit replay authorization, report error retention and conservative cleanup after uncertain termination. Never automatically log application error/panic contents. Keep tracing context around polling and full future/span destruction. Do not install library global subscribers or panic hooks, recreate upstream queue/provisioning/storage engines, or infer publication/deployment permission.

Use a task-local ExecPlan under .agent/PLANS.md for sufficiently complex implementation. Its steps/evidence belong to this bead; it must not become a second backlog. Keep acceptance and status in Beads, behavior contracts in docs/guarantees.md and docs/integrations.md, implemented capability facts in docs/status.md, and executed evidence in the owning Bead. New public APIs need rustdoc and a runnable or doctest example. Add meaningful failure-path tests without weakening existing assertions. Do not overwrite existing migrations or silently break queued/persisted formats.

For code/dependency changes run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh; build cargo build -p batter --features axum --example http_service --locked and run python3 scripts/smoke_http.py --binary target/debug/examples/http_service in default, --signal SIGINT and --deadline modes. Finish backend verification with scripts/jig check test, and run applicable Jig work gates. These local checks do not replace the task-specific subprocess, live DB, upstream compatibility or hosted evidence below. Record exact command, toolchain, platform, lock hash, result and missing prerequisites. Do not call a compile-only or skipped-prerequisite result runtime validation. Existing public integration API availability must be checked against the actual upstream version at implementation time and cited in docs/references.md.

Legacy reference: BTR-070. Audited against commit 9654b2ec1ac9823008968efc2fdb5088fbd2f7f3, docs/roadmap.md, docs/testing.md, docs/integrations.md, docs/operations.md, docs/effect-v4-reconciliation.md, docs/status.md and SECURITY.md. title: Define trusted request metadata and explicit propagation
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Existing HTTP span and renderer correlation is implemented; the remaining gap is trusted request metadata and explicit propagation in the reference root.

## Scope and ownership

Define typed correlation separately from OperationContext and application authority. Consume server-generated correlation from batter-7r3.4 through extensions and explicit arguments; validate any separately retained inbound request/trace metadata without allowing it to select server identity. The application owns authentication and trusted peer/proxy configuration. Default to ignoring forwarded identity from untrusted peers; if proxy trust is supported, its configured peer boundary is explicit. Introduce task-local ergonomics only for a real consumer with absence/spawn semantics, not as a prerequisite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Forged forwarding, trace and request-ID headers cannot select principal, tenant or quota identity; test direct/untrusted input and every trusted-peer mode actually supported.
- Concurrent requests, missing metadata and cancellation do not exchange identity; handlers, failures and nested operations retain the intended correlation.
- Use the existing independent observe_http/request_admission composition and retained first-poll parent/dispatcher behavior; do not duplicate or reopen its closed implementation tasks.
- Any explicit spawned-work helper tests inheritance and absence; arbitrary tokio::spawn remains outside automatic propagation.
- Authorization is exercised through the production reference middleware seam; a correlation identifier is never a capability grant.
- The reference uses the shared request-correlation primitives from batter-7r3.4; generated response/header/body identity agrees while application authority and trusted-peer policy remain separate typed inputs.
- No duplicate server-ID, response-header or infrastructure-rendering implementation remains in reference middleware; application-specific authentication and durable metadata tests remain at their production seams.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

batter-7r3.4 owns reusable trusted server request identity, correlation spans/headers, optional safe infrastructure rendering and readiness/serve composition. Consume that adapter API here instead of copying middleware into the reference. This task continues to own production authentication/trusted-peer policy and explicit propagation into application, quota and durable-submission paths. Correlation is diagnostic data; it must never substitute for principal/tenant authority. Keep the existing command prerequisite batter-kpd and add only the shared adapter prerequisite. The basic adapter remains independently deliverable without the durable reference.

title: Establish reference-service overload and operational evidence
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Production-oriented workload evidence needs the completed reference protocols and diagnostics, together with real transport/transitive-shutdown limits.

## Scope and ownership

Measure the reference under reproducible overload using the selected PostgreSQL/provider protocol and application config. Justify pool/admission/worker capacity together. Include slow/unavailable diagnostics and observe resource use, latency, rejection, error and shutdown behavior. Preserve uncertainty and avoid invented universal performance targets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dataset, environment, limits and workload are reproducible; results include latency distributions, overload/errors and shutdown outcomes.
- Pool/admission/worker and observation resource bounds are measured together; diagnostics reveal saturation without sensitive labels or changing domain outcomes.
- Selected database/provider semantics and uncertainty are explicit; external-effect and attempt counts retain the reference protocol meaning.
- Review dependencies/security against the exact application lockfile and record findings separately from publication. Local/hosted evidence is scoped honestly.

## Code and evidence entrypoints

- examples/reference-service/ (new unpublished application package)
- docs/integrations.md
- docs/testing.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/validation.md

## Verification and governing constraints

For code/dependency changes, run bash scripts/verify.sh and RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh. Rebuild cargo build -p batter-axum --example http_service --locked and run python3 scripts/smoke_http.py --binary target/debug/examples/http_service in default, --signal SIGINT, --deadline, --warn-filter, and --warn-filter --deadline profiles. Finish backend work with scripts/jig check test and applicable Jig work gates. These commands do not substitute for this task's real database/provider/contract acceptance. Record exact versions, platform, prerequisites, commands and outcomes in docs/validation.md; missing integration prerequisites fail the explicit target rather than silently passing. Read AGENTS.md, agent-map.md and the nearest package guide. New public APIs need rustdoc and an example; update the relevant contract, implemented-status row and owning Bead. Keep library domain errors concrete, cleanup explicitly awaited, Unix-only scope, and upstream queue/provisioning ownership intact. Do not commit, publish or deploy without an explicit request.

## Design evidence

Re-audited against commit 22848ea on 2026-09-09. A permit count does not bound scans, waiter memory, database locks or diagnostics; this is a measured application outcome. The retrospective sample establishes failure mechanisms, not defect rates or current application bugs. See docs/design-evidence.md for the anonymized rationale and implemented baseline. Delivery authority remains this Bead; historical ExecPlans are not another backlog.


## Dependencies and consumers

Blocked by: batter-4qc — Specify and test HTTP handler panic behavior; batter-u0m — Test HTTP connection lifetimes through drain and shutdown; batter-953 — Exercise cancellation and admission races under sustained scheduling; batter-zu8 — Prove component descendant and uncertain-termination contracts; batter-fvz — Bound non-yielding lifecycle tests with a subprocess watchdog; batter-fms — Prove atomicity, idempotency and durable lifetime with real PostgreSQL; batter-97p — Compose upstream admission and sanitized observation in the reference API; batter-8jr — Provide application-root exporter setup and ordered flush

title: Retain all fixture failures through partial acquisition and teardown
description:
## Outcome and rationale

Fixture failures must retain their actual causes without deleting a database while native pool shutdown remains unresolved. The inspected harness lease queues database cleanup on Drop, so dropping a skipped finalizer is not retention.

## Scope and ownership

Extend the minimal probe fixtures from batter-4jz with an explicitly driven cleanup owner holding pools and leases. Start/retain that owner before yielding a cancellable waiter; waiter cancellation does not drop the lease or stop cleanup. After a bounded observation timeout, keep ownership in the fixture/suite driver and expose a pending result that can be awaited again. Do not call defer_cleanup or drop a captured lease before all connections close. Ordinary owner loss/runtime death has no cleanup-completion guarantee and must be documented/tested rather than described as safe skipping. Prove these mechanics without depending on a future application router; production composition fidelity belongs to batter-8q8.1, batter-8q8.2 and batter-fms.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hold a real connection through the close observation deadline. Verify the database/lease is still retained while the cleanup owner remains live, then release the connection and observe Pool::close completion before lease cleanup. Cancelled waiters can resume observation of the same owner/result.
- SQLx 0.9 close returns (); distinguish timeout, cancelled observation and cleanup-owner join failure from a native returned error. Do not fabricate an SQLx close error or claim quiescence from dropped close futures.
- Preserve the original body failure together with actual cleanup failures. Awaited consuming lease cleanup and deferred-queue failure cases use their real separate paths/resources; do not assume the same consumed lease produces both errors. Synthetic boundary errors may test aggregation only when labelled as such.
- Continue independent cleanup after failure while retaining unresolved dependent resources. Explicit upstream defer is used only after connection quiescence; separately await deferred drain, including external mode where harness shutdown is a no-op.
- Assertion error, unwinding panic, cancelled waiter, partial acquisition and cleanup-owner loss have bounded tests naming what remains owned and driven. A pending outcome is not clean reuse; ordinary lease Drop is not a no-op and cannot satisfy skipped deletion.
- For the adapter from batter-7r3.2 (available through batter-4jz), test native SQLx PoolConnection::detach as the negative control. Use a separately budgeted observation connection outside the closing one-slot pool to track retired backend identities. Retain the lease until those sessions are observed quiescent too; Pool::close covers only tracked connections. Failed observation retains an unfinished owner/report instead of releasing the database.
- Reuse existing Script/finish for body and script-verification failures where applicable; shared adapter-owned result/cleanup mechanics are consumed by the minimal probe fixture. External adoption belongs to batter-7r3.6, without a reverse completion dependency.
- Generic batter-test-support gains no harness/foundation dependency. Reference consumers later keep actual config, router and transaction paths with substitutions only at selected external boundaries.

## Operational reuse scope (2026-09-09)

Reuse the existing generic Script and finish semantics for application/body-plus-verification failures instead of adding another assertion-result convention. ## Outcome and rationale

Successful schema conversion and generated client compilation do not prove that the wire contract preserves domain meaning or matches runtime routes.

title: Implement the reference command and atomic transactional submission
description:
## Outcome and rationale

A command is incomplete if it commits its business mutation independently of required durable work, or loses exact resource identity when a retry arrives.

## Scope and ownership

Implement a small generic reference command and query in examples/reference-service. The minimal scenario is delivery of a versioned generic record: a record has an application-owned owner and monotonically changing generation; POST /records/{record_id}/deliveries accepts expected_generation, an idempotency_key and a bounded payload, and GET /deliveries/{delivery_id} projects persisted state. Canonical identity binds the trusted owner, record, generation and payload. The first command creates a stable delivery identifier and upstream submission; exact replay preserves them. Initial records and replacement generations may be prepared by verified fixture/admin operations, not new public product features. The later provider task owns execution states; the command initially exposes accepted/conflict/uncertain outcomes without fabricating execution success. One native SQLx transaction owns the business record and upstream submission. Model a stable command identity, application-owned idempotency key and canonical payload comparison; give the target an explicit generation so stale work can be rejected. Preserve concrete success/conflict/uncertain-commit outcomes. Pass one OperationContext budget through pool acquisition and command execution with an explicit connection/transaction disposition policy. Use the config constructors from batter-5pm. Forward-only application migrations and upstream compatibility checks precede readiness. Do not add a repository abstraction, transaction retry manager or second queue.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The runnable command shares one visible native transaction for the business write and upstream submission; a query exposes durable identity and actual state.
- Request idempotency is scoped to the authenticated owner. Same-key/same-payload replay preserves identity; conflicting payload stays a concrete conflict. Another owner cannot alias that command by reusing its key; replay and status lookup enforce the same ownership as initial submission. Canonical comparison binds owner, target generation and meaningful payload; retention is explicit.
- The command targets the exact record/generation; stale ownership never silently applies to a replacement. Public success projection comes from a closed domain state representation.
- One total budget reaches pool acquisition and database work. Timing out a client future does not prove rollback or connection disposal; uncertain disposition is represented and documented.
- Commit acknowledgement loss remains an uncertain outcome with a query/reconciliation path; no automatic transaction replay is introduced.
- Production router/root uses the configured constructors and application-owned authentication seam; tests may replace a provider/auth boundary, but must not compile production authorization out.
- Focused checks accompany implementation; real transaction/concurrency proof is owned by batter-8q8.1 and combined acceptance by batter-fms.
