title: Adopt protected startup and pool ownership in canonical consumers
description:
# Delivery D

Status: planned, not implemented. Own code, tests, docs and evidence together.

## Owning delivery graph

Epic batter-lp2 owns this outcome. A=batter-lp2.1, B=batter-lp2.2, C=batter-lp2.3, D=batter-lp2.4.
Blocking edges: B depends on A; D depends on A/B/C. A and C are independently
ready. Parent-child grouping and related coordination are not blocking edges.
Facade relocation batter-tmx, broad adoption batter-7r3.6, fixture pool profiles
batter-7r3.8 and closed documentation convergence batter-fbd are related only.
Resolve current source paths at implementation; preserve one foundation type
identity and do not close or broaden unrelated Beads.

## D: Adopt the protected path in runnable consumers

Outcome: the reference root, HTTP example, PostgreSQL lifecycle example and finite
pool consumer use the new APIs; public guidance and independently evaluated agent
implementation agree on the canonical ownership path.

Depends on A, B and C. Entry points: examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs,
examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs, crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs,
related package tests; docs/usage, integrations, guarantees, architecture, status,
validation and source references. Preserve current batter-fbd documentation edits.

Replace the reference's manual signal install/select/transfer with builder policy.
Move PostgreSQL demo signal selection before acquisition by library startup policy.
Use slot-consuming native pool creation where code now clones/registers pool close.
Use the protected registration target for Axum and prepared Runledger.
Keep stage metadata, schemas, authentication, settings/PG* validation, native probes,
provider absence and without_readiness_approval semantics application-owned.
Do not remove the deliberate long-running demo component merely to force use of
Command; changing a service demonstration into a finite command changes its purpose.

Update canonical documentation with complete compiling compositions. Show old APIs
only as compatibility/escape paths with precise obligations. Avoid duplicate large
agent guides; contracts live in owning public docs, guide files route to them.
Coordinate paths/imports with facade work if it has landed; do not force that work
to block this delivery or copy historical source files over newer implementations.

Acceptance scenarios:
1. Real reference startup SIGTERM/SIGINT before DB initialization completes follows
   awaited failure cleanup, including stalled initialization and waiter loss.
2. Running HTTP behavior and all five smoke modes preserve prior status/headers,
   readiness/drain, deadlines and sanitized exit diagnostics.
3. Reference keeps readiness unapproved and no production startup witness jobs.
4. Existing live SQLx/reference exact case inventory remains covered, with source
   identities, toolchain and actual platform recorded.
5. New consumer task starts from behavioral requirements/public guidance, no fixed
   ownership signatures, hidden library tests or previous repair transcript.
6. Retain the agent's first source before compiling; record compiler diagnostics,
   repairs, guidance ambiguities and abandoned approaches without inflating success.
7. Independent oracles cover real SIGTERM startup cleanup, native query plus later
   failure, and constrained adapter registration. A subsequent modification adds
   a second dependency and startup stage without rebuilding lifecycle protocols.
8. A separate fresh agent reviews implementability of the standalone delivery task;
   same-agent modification is not another independent sample.
9. Report number of agent tasks and exact conditions, never a general reliability
   percentage. Planning prototypes do not replace final production acceptance.
10. All code/doc/verification requirements below pass before task closure.
## D — actual consumer migration

### Consumer anchors and intended substitutions

[`runtime::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:90) currently owns manual signal routing.
Its `Startup::new` begins at line 95; manual installation, selection, and transfer occur inside the initializer.
[`register_pool`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:147) manually publishes a lazy pool close.
[`register_health`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:162) currently requires `&mut Supervisor`.
[`postgres-lifecycle::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs:51) connects before installing signals.
Its [`serve`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs:92) fixes the initializer's legacy scope type.
[`http_service::run`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/crates/batter-axum/examples/http_service.rs:171) uses the legacy startup projection.
Its dependency helper at line 42 takes `&mut Supervisor`; line 192 obtains a handle through that scope.
[`Session::new`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/retirement/session.rs:26) is the actual finite pool consumer.
It already runs under `CommandScope` and manually registers a native lazy pool.
Its physical-session replacement guard and fixed one-slot configuration are operational requirements.

### Required A/B interfaces at the D boundary

D consumes `batter::startup::ProtectedStartupScope` through `Startup::scoped`.
The protected start result is `StartingSupervisor<InitializationError<E>>`.
The protected builder supplies `.with_unix_signals(name) -> Self`.
`InitializationError<E>` retains `Application(E)`, `Signals(SignalRegistrationError)`, and repeated-policy failure.
D must use A's delivered non-exhaustive envelope rather than extending existing `StartupCause`.
The scope supplies `stage`, direct `reserve_cleanup`, and `registration`.
It supplies no unrestricted supervisor or newly introduced context accessor.
Adapters expose `batter_axum::register_http_in` and `batter_runledger::register_in`.
They accept the sealed registration target and share implementation with legacy entrypoints.
If an A/B signature differs from this agreed boundary, report to its owning Bead and block D;
do not implement predecessor API repair inside the consumer migration.
Do not compensate by adding scope escape methods or rebuilding signal routing in D.

Use these application-private helper shapes where useful:

```rust
fn register_pool(
    scope: &mut batter::startup::ProtectedStartupScope,
    settings: &RootSettings,
) -> Result<sqlx::PgPool, BoxError>;

fn register_health(
    registration: batter::registration::Registration<'_>,
    pool: sqlx::PgPool,
) -> Result<HealthReader<OperationError<batter_sqlx::SqlxFailure>>, BoxError>;
```

A concrete borrowed registration parameter keeps authority visible without another application trait.
Reborrow successive helpers using the delivered registration method.
Capture readiness handles and native operation contexts at the composition root before moving the supervisor.
Do not manufacture a second parent deadline to work around a scope borrow.

### Migration sequence

1. Confirm A/B/C signatures and their compatibility tests before editing application roots.
2. Migrate the reference pool helper to direct scope reservation plus `batter_sqlx::pool_in`.
3. Preserve `RootSettings::connect_options_from_process` and `pool_options` as the native-option boundary.
4. Replace reference startup with `Startup::scoped(...).with_unix_signals("signals")`.
5. Remove application-owned listener installation, `tokio::select!`, and listener transfer from that initializer.
6. Preserve application stage names for pool acquisition, schema initialization, HTTP bind, and worker registration.
7. Remove or reclassify the old signal-install stage; synchronous policy failures precede application stages.
8. Register health through `Registration`, HTTP through `register_http_in`, and prepared Runledger through `register_in`.
9. Preserve the empty production registry and `.without_readiness_approval()`.
10. Keep schema initialization, authenticated routes, settings validation, and native health sampling unchanged.

11. Migrate the PostgreSQL lifecycle `serve` callback bound to `ProtectedStartupScope`.
12. Select Unix policy on its startup builder before the synchronous `start` boundary.
13. Parse its application-owned `DATABASE_URL` into native `PgConnectOptions` outside `pool_in`.
14. Keep parsing errors before pool construction; do not create a new settings framework for this demo.
15. Replace eager pool construction and manual finalization with reservation and `pool_in`.
16. Retain the explicit bounded probe before registering dependent application work.
17. Document the changed acquisition timing: return from construction is now lazy; the explicit probe establishes connectivity.
18. Preserve the deliberate long-running `application` component and its real startup acknowledgement.
19. Remove only obsolete example-local signal helper calls; retain compatibility helpers still used elsewhere.
20. Migrate actual live-test setup into the new initializer rather than precreating pools outside ownership.

21. Migrate HTTP startup and capture its shutdown/readiness handle before moving the supervisor.
22. Convert its health helper to registration authority and use `register_http_in` for listener ownership.
23. Select the same Unix policy on the builder; preserve router, middleware, configuration, and exit rendering.
24. Migrate retirement `Session::new` by passing its completed `PgPoolOptions` and native options to `pool_in`.
25. Preserve one connection, zero minimum, disabled idle/max lifetime, acquire timeout, and `search_path`.
26. Preserve the entire `after_connect` replacement guard, its atomics, and its fixed diagnostic.
27. Do not change retirement verification, transaction boundaries, cancellation, or separate readback ownership.
28. Run the physical replacement regression through the reference runner after this finite-consumer change.

### Application error and compatibility handling

Reference [`RuntimeStartupFailure::startup`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:65) publicly returns the legacy typed error.
Silently changing that return type would violate the staged public-contract policy.
Preserve that type and accessor for legacy clients.
Add the distinct ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure wrapper for the canonical root's
expanded error envelope. D preserves old type/accessor source compatibility, not
runtime::run's old boxed-error downcast behavior. The intended interface is:

```rust
pub struct ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure(/* private retained error */);

impl ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure {
    pub fn startup(
        &self,
    ) -> &batter::startup::StartupError<
        batter::startup::InitializationError<InitializationFailure>
    >;
}
```

Implement fixed `Display` and `Debug`, with `Error::source` retaining the actual protected startup error.
Document that `run` still returns `Result<(), BoxError>` but deliberately changes
its startup-error downcast target to ProtectedRuntimeStartupFailure. This is an
explicit reference-root behavioral cutover, not a claim of unchanged downcasts.
Migrate examples/reference-service/tests/support/startup_process.rs accordingly.
Search downstream examples and tests for old downcasts and migrate those intended to follow the protected root.
Retain a compiled fixture for the original public wrapper accessor.
Do not fabricate an application error for a signal-installation failure to preserve an old downcast.
Protected application failures unwrap through `StartupCause::Failed(InitializationError::Application(...))`.
Retain native SQLx errors, native listener IO errors, cleanup outcomes, and destruction panic independently.
Update PostgreSQL example test helpers that downcast the formerly legacy startup error.
[`check_shutdown`](/home/aa/Documents/batter/examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs:143) is a report checker, not a report-producing accessor.
Tests needing detailed shutdown assertions retain the actual outcome/report before applying that checker.

## Live inventory and environment ownership

### Existing SQLx and PostgreSQL example inventory

The SQLx runner currently owns these ten exact ignored names:

```text
blocked_cancellation_releases_capacity
```

## Selected architecture

1. A concrete borrowed Registration capability contains private access to the
   existing Supervisor registration operations. It offers component registration,
   managed-adapter registration and finalizer reservation, never start,
   run_until, cleanup extraction, replacement or a conversion to Supervisor.
2. A small sealed RegistrationTarget trait exposes only a reborrowed Registration.
   New adapter entrypoints register_http_in and register_in accept it, so protected
   scopes pass directly. Preserve the original adapter signatures; changing them
   to generics breaks existing DerefMut coercion callers. Both names share the
   same registration implementation. Applications need not implement the trait.
3. Introduce additive Startup::scoped and ProtectedStartupScope over the existing
   engine. Preserve existing Startup::new and StartupScope for source compatibility
   as explicitly lower-level paths. The canonical new scope has direct
   reserve_cleanup and registration access, no unrestricted supervisor accessor.
   Its start result uses InitializationError<E> from its first delivery, so later
   signal support does not change the protected path's public error type.
4. An opt-in Unix signal policy belongs to protected startup. Its configuration
   is inert. Starting synchronously validates/reserves the signal name and
   installs SIGTERM/SIGINT before returning the startup owner; the owned engine
   observes reception during initialization and carries sources into running
   supervision without a fallible application handoff.
5. A synchronous SQLx pool constructor consumes an already validated CleanupSlot
   plus native PgPoolOptions/PgConnectOptions, constructs the native pool and
   registers close before returning. Name it batter_sqlx::pool_in. Connectivity
   checks remain explicit native queries or the existing bounded probe. The async
   alternative was tested but is not selected for this delivery.
6. Real example adoption and a fresh public-guidance consumer task complete the
   delivery. Library tests alone do not establish discovery or modification
   usability. No future adapter, publication or production readiness is implied.

- Never log native error or panic contents through automatic diagnostics.

- Registered finalization remains awaited, bounded and LIFO.
- Borrowed waiter cancellation changes no ownership; owner loss requests drain.
- Runtime death, process kill and non-yielding code retain existing limitations.
- Pool close does not certify server-session termination or rollback.
- Types do not stop arbitrary tokio::spawn, leaked handles or remote effects.
- No existing database migrations or durable delivery formats change.

title: Avoid repeating relation-owner authority for every column
description:
Verified low-severity residual from the comprehensive review-fix loop; below its medium repair threshold. Claude identified the mechanism; parent static triage confirmed it in the final working files.

crates/batter-sqlx/src/verification/authority/requests.rs::inspect_relation_columns passes the relation owner into inspect_acl_object_parts for every column. privileges.rs::IndexedAcl::actual_for supplies all four column privileges and their grant options for that owner, and inspect_acl_object_parts_collect also adds Ownership. An otherwise denied owner therefore produces nine owner-derived findings per column in addition to relation-level findings. About 1,000 owned ten-column tables can fit the 10,000-column capture bound but exceed the 100,000-finding bound, converting useful ownership diagnostics into EvaluationCapacity. This is diagnostic amplification, not a false pass; capacity errors remain conservative.

Remediation: report owner-implied authority at its owning relation without repeating it for every column. Preserve independently granted column privileges/grant options, explicit column policy exceptions and PUBLIC findings. Acceptance: a multi-column owner fixture retains its relation ownership violation without linear duplicate owner diagnostics, and a near-capacity fixture preserves actionable findings; explicit column-only grants remain detected.

Causal group R3; pinned working-tree HEAD ff507dcf48c688bbc31d99a517cfd5888de5910a. No repair attempt in this loop.

title: Declare and verify PostgreSQL transaction timeouts in session profiles
description:
Outcome: let a consumer declare idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and transaction_timeout in PgSessionProfile, with library-owned application and verification throughout the existing profiled pool, atomic and snapshot paths. Ownership belongs to batter-sqlx; timeout values remain application policy.

Audit correction (2026-09-22): the originally filed claim that PgConnectOptions startup timeouts become zero after DISCARD ALL is disproved on PostgreSQL 18.6 with SQLx 0.9.0 and the current Batter implementation. Startup options remain the session reset defaults. Values set later by SET/set_config are reset; PgProfiledPool also intentionally replaces supplied pool hooks. A generic fixture using after_connect session policy therefore loses settings that the profile cannot express, whereas the production-style startup-options path retains them. Preserve this distinction in the regression and documentation.

Confirmed gap: profile.rs declares/applies/verifies only statement_timeout and lock_timeout; with_setting rejects both missing built-in GUCs. No declarative profile contract can establish or revalidate the two transaction settings. A profiled atomic callback can SET both to zero and still complete successfully because those values are absent from verification. A connection-options workaround cannot supply that missing verification contract.

Affected source: the downstream pin 70cc6a05be6857aca6ea2f5f127258e75e673d8c and audited HEAD d28a500dd10deeb957e32d478c4f85ca10e2e13d have identical profile.rs. Relevant entrypoints are crates/batter-sqlx/src/profile.rs, profiled_pool.rs, atomic.rs::validate and snapshot.rs::inspect_with_profile.

Limits: idle-in-transaction timeout bounds an idle interval; transaction_timeout bounds transaction duration. These server settings do not cancel an arbitrary Rust callback or release a held local pool lease. Existing OperationContext-owned runners govern cooperative local deadlines. Preserve uncertain commit/rollback outcomes and the distinction between local retirement and observed backend termination. Arbitrary SQL remains an escape hatch; verification is not a sandbox.
design:
Implement as one cohesive adapter task; no prerequisite delivery Bead was identified. Do not add core dependencies, provisioning, migrations, reset callbacks, retries or a replacement transaction owner.

Recommended compatibility path: add a canonical constructor requiring all four timeout selections (a seven-argument constructor is sufficient; no framework or typestate hierarchy is needed). Keep fields private and reuse the exact whole-millisecond 0..=i32::MAX validation. Zero explicitly disables the selected timeout; nonzero selection is application policy. Preserve the existing constructor's source compatibility and inherited reset-default behavior for the two previously undeclared settings. Mark that constructor as the weaker compatibility path in rustdoc, and lead examples with the complete declaration. Internally distinguish undeclared legacy fields from explicit zero: silently defaulting new fields to zero would disable existing connection/role/database budgets. API spelling is an implementation choice; the complete canonical declaration and unchanged legacy behavior are acceptance requirements.

Apply the new declared values in PgSessionProfile::apply after reset and before BEGIN; verify numeric millisecond values through pg_catalog.pg_settings in the shared verify method. Existing after_connect, before_acquire and after_release hooks, atomic validation and snapshot validation must use the same fields. Keep with_setting's prohibition, including mixed-case spellings. Preserve redacted setup errors with retained native causes, failed/cancelled setup retirement, poisoning on detected drift, and existing acknowledged/uncertain disposition.

Version contract: transaction_timeout was introduced in PostgreSQL 17; PostgreSQL 18 is the native verification baseline. A complete declaration requires the parameter to exist, including when explicitly disabled. Missing/unsupported parameters must fail setup before callback access, never silently skip the declared budget. Legacy construction must not acquire a new parameter/version requirement. Use native setup failure or an explicit capability check; do not claim older-version execution without evidence.

ADR-010 assessment: invalid precision/range is locally rejectable; complete canonical timeout selection belongs in construction; reset/apply/verification ordering belongs to the adapter. Timeout selection, including zero and relative values, is application policy, not the core parent/child deadline invariant. PostgreSQL precedence and termination are upstream behavior. SQL mutation between checks, backend disappearance and a pending Rust callback are remote/execution limits, not locally provable permanent guarantees. No repeated repair loop or fresh-agent usability evaluation was executed by this audit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A canonical declarative profile requires explicit statement, lock, idle-in-transaction and total-transaction timeout selections, validates exact whole milliseconds and PostgreSQL's signed-32-bit range before I/O, and treats zero as explicit disable. Existing constructor callers retain prior behavior; omission must not silently disable inherited settings. Rustdoc and a generic compiling example explain the compatibility boundary.
2. Shared apply/verify enforce both new declared values after reset, before work and at existing atomic/snapshot validation boundaries. All three PgProfiledPool hooks retain ownership. with_setting cannot override them; no caller hook or paired reset step is required. Detected drift cannot yield ordinary successful completion.
3. Offline cases cover each new timeout independently: zero, one millisecond, maximum, overflow and fractional milliseconds; built-in/mixed-case override rejection; redacted formatting. Live PG18 cases distinguish startup options surviving reset from SET/hook values being cleared, then prove explicit profile values override different startup/reset defaults, including explicit zero overriding nonzero defaults and legacy construction preserving existing defaults.
4. Live cases cover initial connection, reused checkout and after_release restoration before try_acquire, plus profiled atomic and snapshot paths. Change each timeout independently during scope SQL to prove revalidation rejects drift and retains the terminal cause/disposition. Exercise setup failure/cancellation retirement with existing controls and preserve retained native errors and redaction.
5. Independently observe server behavior: idle termination while awaiting the client and total-transaction termination despite individually short statements. Use bounded polling/observation and cleanup, not only SHOW or elapsed sleeps. Preserve the documented fact that server termination alone does not cancel Rust work or release a still-held pool slot. Keep deadline/cancellation and ambiguous commit handling conservative; add no automatic retry.
6. Document the PG17 parameter introduction, PG18 executed baseline, explicit-zero semantics, timeout precedence and fail-closed unsupported-parameter behavior. Record primary sources in docs/references.md. Do not advertise unexecuted platform/version coverage.
7. Update the SQLx contract/README, relevant guarantees/integration text, implemented-status row, failure tests and this Bead. Register added live cases in scripts/sqlx_live.py's exact inventory; keep .jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json input scopes synchronized if new inputs require changes. Use generic scenarios and external fixture provisioning.
8. Delivery evidence must include adapter offline/live verification, required final fresh api:test/Jig gates, both Rust 1.98.1 and exact 1.94.0 verification matrices/rustdoc and the required built HTTP smokes per AGENTS.md/docs/testing.md, reusing only qualifying receipts. Label fresh-agent evaluations proposed/unexecuted unless actually run. No commit or publication is authorized by this audit.
notes:
Audit 2026-09-22: implementable with the corrected scope/design/acceptance above; implementation remains open. Only this Bead/export is changed by the audit. No production source, dependency or downstream edits were made.

Executed evidence: isolated disposable PostgreSQL 18.6 container on Linux; Rust 1.98.1; SQLx 0.9.0; standalone temporary Rust consumer against local batter-sqlx. PGOPTIONS/psql control showed setting=reset_val=10000/15000 with source=client before and after DISCARD ALL. Rust probe asserted: (a) PgProfiledPool checkout with startup options returns (10s,15s); (b) reset_and_apply clears after_connect SET values to (0,0) on default-zero server; (c) a supplied hook is replaced and omitted profile values remain (0,0); (d) run_atomic_profiled with initial nonzero startup values accepts SET of both omitted fields to zero; (e) an independent pg_stat_activity observer sees a backend disappear under a 250ms idle-in-transaction timeout while the held one-slot pool still has size=1, idle=0, and try_acquire=None. Probe has a 30s outer watchdog and closes all owned connections/pools.

Source evidence for downstream diagnosis: production construction adds PgConnectOptions::options, while fixture pool construction sets values in after_connect then copies those options into PgProfiledPool, which replaces hooks. The fixture assertion expects zeros; a separate server-timeout contract expects nonzero values. These differ and must not be treated as proof that startup options are erased. Consumer source was inspected read-only; its full tests were not run. Private consumer names/paths are intentionally excluded from this upstream task.

Primary sources checked: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-reset.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/sql-discard.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-client.html ; https://www.postgresql.org/docs/17/release-17.html . title: Reject non-finite Unix process watchdog bounds
description:
## Observed behavior

`scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` accepts non-finite `timeout` and
`reap_allowance` values. Its validation checks only `<= 0`, so both positive
infinity and NaN reach deadline arithmetic in `_run_owned_process`,
`Capture.observe_until`, and `_settle`.

On 2026-09-09 on Darwin 25.6.0 arm64 with Python 3.14.7, this repository-root
control returned successful `ProcessOutcome` values instead of raising
`ValueError` for all four cases:

```python
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("inf"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=float("nan"), reap_allowance=1, output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("inf"), output_limit=1024)
run_process(["/usr/bin/true"], timeout=1, reap_allowance=float("nan"), output_limit=1024)
```

The focused `test_scheduling_process.py` suite passed all 24 tests, confirming
that the current test inventory does not reject these values. The sibling
`parallel_process.run_parallel` already requires finite positive bounds and has
an infinity/NaN regression.

## Expected behavior

The bounded Unix process owner should reject every non-finite or non-positive
duration before launching a child. A malformed bound must not be able to turn a
watchdog or termination/reap allowance into an unbounded wait.

## Affected code and likely impact

- `scripts/scheduling_process.py::run_process` validates `timeout` and
  `reap_allowance` incompletely.
- `_run_owned_process` uses `started + timeout`; `Capture.observe_until` cannot
  reach its `remaining <= 0` exit with infinity or NaN.
- `_settle` similarly derives its cleanup deadline from `reap_allowance`.

This is lower-impact because callers are repository-owned test tools with
normally constant values. If a future CLI/configured caller supplies a
non-finite value, however, a hung child can hang local or CI verification
instead of producing bounded failure evidence.

## Verification limitation

The control used `/usr/bin/true` to prove invalid values are accepted without
deliberately launching a permanently hanging child. It therefore did not wait
through the unbounded failure mode. No Linux, hosted CI, or other Python version
was exercised for this finding.
acceptance_criteria: run_process rejects NaN, infinity, zero, and negative timeout/reap allowances before spawning; focused regressions cover both fields and preserve existing bounded success, timeout, interruption, overflow, and reap behavior.

Prove the high-level PostgreSQL verification path in one authorized real
same-stack consumer, remove its duplicated generic machinery, and record an

## Scope

`.agent/plans/batter-7r3.6-compact-verification-adoption.md`. Exact consumer paths,
commands, revisions, method/error contracts, and LOC inventories are in the
authorized private companion; keep public upstream scenarios generic.

Before upstream API freeze, use an uncommitted local-path prototype for all four
real profiles. Compare compiled policies to independent pre-existing low-level
oracles and new grant effects to old provisioning-script effects. Delete the
translator and scripts recoverably in the prototype and reject an API that does
not reduce the replacement-inclusive responsibility. Then run Batter's bounded
comprehensive low-severity review-fix loop. Pin only an authorized immutable
remote revision, restore all Git dependencies together, and run the consumer's

## Acceptance

- All four profiles are readable grouped application data and one compiled
  representation feeds verification, test provisioning, and deterministic
  render-only operator output.
- Independent low-level policy oracles and old-script semantic controls prove
  the new manifest rather than using it as its own sole oracle.
- Schema, role, and queue public methods, startup order, error categories,
  missing/excess behavior, lock-only columns, routines, sequences, PUBLIC,
  inheritance/SET/ADMIN reachability, ownership, and real business operations
  remain covered.
- The render command runs before ordinary application configuration while
  preserving earlier transport dispatch, performs no external I/O except
  buffered stdout, and uses an explicit transactional `psql -X` workflow whose
  tested failures cannot commit a prefix.
- The generic translator, duplicate queue adapter/catalog checks, and four
  hand-maintained grant scripts are removed, with all live references updated.
- The replacement-inclusive consumer responsibility is strictly smaller than its
  recomputed pre-adoption baseline. Historical measurements, Batter growth,
  tests/docs, and generated SQL are reported separately.
- Both repositories' required local gates and independent comprehensive
  low-severity review-fix loops converge on final fingerprints. An immutable
  upstream revision is remotely resolvable and all consumer Batter pins match it.
- Generic adoption evidence is appended without claiming deployment, hosted CI,
  release, or a second adopter that did not occur.

title: Make checked shutdown completion propagate operational failures
description:
# Checked shutdown completion

## Outcome

A canonical owned-process completion call such as `running.wait_checked().await?;` or `running.shutdown_checked().await?;` propagates every unsuccessful shutdown without a second report inspection. Successful callers may retain the completed report for application-specific checks. Planning baseline: `7f3248f08e70de83da89d62cbdc94a1ab8befd1a` (2026-09-22). This epic is the canonical cross-task design; child Beads own acceptance, status and dependencies. No implementation or test execution is claimed by this plan. Source-level downstream audit added 2026-09-22; the two application checkouts were inspected without changing them.

## Scope

Include RunningSupervisor, UnapprovedSupervisor and SupervisorObserver checked completion, an opaque success value, explicit raw-report observation, compatibility guidance, focused regressions, public consumer adoption, generic regression recipes derived from two actual downstreams, isolated candidate compatibility rehearsals and required verification.

Exclude changes to shutdown budgets, readiness, admission, drain/cancel/join/cleanup execution, Startup construction, acquisition protocols, finite-command completion, caller-owned run_until output, native Runledger supervision, permanent downstream dependency/pin updates, publication and deployment. Temporary candidate source overrides in disposable consumer copies are verification inputs, not adopted pins. Preserve Unix-only scope, native Rust/Tokio, facade/core type identity, report retention and redaction. No new task runtime, background waiter, logging policy or general result framework.

## Current-state evidence

- Fact: `crates/batter-core/src/lifecycle/driver.rs::DriverOutcome` is Result of SharedShutdownReport or shared JoinError. All five owned owner/observer wait/shutdown methods return it; an Ok report can be unsuccessful.
- Fact: the same file already defines ShutdownFailure::{Report, Coordinator} and check_shutdown. `lifecycle/report.rs::ShutdownReport::is_success` rejects empty supervisors, non-stopped direct tasks, abort requests, unsuccessful/pending managed outcomes, unjoined tasks and unsuccessful cleanup. Preserve this classifier; forced cancellation alone is not an additional failure rule.
- Fact: `tests/process_ownership/report_usage.rs` requires the exact unused_must_use lint and preserves shared report/error identity. `tests/driver_observer.rs` covers last-owner drop, coordinator panic and runtime loss. Binding a raw report bypasses the lint; it does not classify shutdown.
- Fact: `examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs::check_application_shutdown` clones the raw report, invokes check_shutdown, then requires a postgres.pool record. This is a real use for successful evidence; required-resource presence remains application policy.
- Fact: `crates/batter/examples/{worker,http_service,quota_service,process_owned}.rs` and `examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs` manually classify or aggregate completion. process_owned must finish shutdown even if its body fails; a premature question-mark would regress it. Its current failure branch drops both causes after logging booleans, so the migration must improve retention with a small private application aggregate rather than preserve that loss.
- Fact: prior report-lint and protected-startup delivery is closed (`batter-66g`, `batter-lp2.4`). No existing open checked-completion delivery task was found in tracker inspection.
- Fact (service and worker consumer): checkout `4ed212978fa2534d550120dbfb9c9a18dde1cbc5`, Batter/native graph pin `70cc6a05be6857aca6ea2f5f127258e75e673d8c`. `crates/*-process/src/serve.rs::ServeProcess::wait` (lines 100-111) logs the report before check_shutdown into anyhow; it serves both public and administrator binaries. `apps/*-api/src/runtime.rs::WorkerProcess::wait` (lines 39-65) separately handles readiness rejection, readiness timeout plus requested shutdown, and normal completion. `log_worker_shutdown` (lines 69-78) logs unsuccessful reports too. Existing `serve_tests.rs::process_exit_rejects_component_failures_and_reports_skipped_cleanup` downcasts ShutdownFailure and checks skipped cleanup; worker native-timeout tests inspect concrete settlement and prevent pool closure. Unrelated frontend edits were present; inspected backend sources were committed.
- Fact (shared service runtime consumer): clean checkout `de1f492daea3e758d73c12a35dff183382af79bc`, Batter pin `cf3db6fc227c8e5ddf4386d4cd9c87f9e8c47056` with a matching batter-sqlx source patch. `crates/*-runtime/src/lib.rs::serve_with_authority` (completion at lines 260-262) already calls check_shutdown into anyhow; both binaries map Err to ExitCode::FAILURE. Maintenance tests ensure in-flight future destruction before resource cleanup and no work after stop. The Docker smoke checks successful signal exit, not injected failed cleanup. Locate the completion call by symbol/search if the private helper is renamed.
- Fact: both applications already propagate failed reports; this epic removes their paired check, not a demonstrated false-success exit in either application. Both use anyhow, beyond the original plan's BoxError-only external recipe. The lifecycle driver/report source at the first pin and lifecycle/startup subtree at the second match the inspected Batter baseline; source pins still must be replaced for candidate verification.
- Fact: direct top-level ShutdownFailure formatting is redacted, but its Coordinator source is the retained native JoinError. The shared service binaries use Debug on anyhow errors, which traverses causes; this audit does not establish redaction of those chains or native panic-hook output. Existing source identity must not be erased to make a redaction assertion pass.
- Inference: moving existing classification into completion methods removes one paired-call obligation without changing execution ownership. Better agent convergence remains unmeasured.
- Unknown: final source state and available Linux/macOS/live PostgreSQL prerequisites at execution time. Each child executor rechecks its affected sources. T-02 owns pin/graph controls and candidate rehearsals below; a baseline/prerequisite failure remains explicit outstanding candidate evidence. Live execution is separately labelled and never inferred from compilation.

## Decisions and design

D-01 — Additive compatibility stage (chosen plan direction). Add wait_checked to both owner types and SupervisorObserver, and shutdown_checked to both owner types. Return a Result with ShutdownSuccess on success and ShutdownFailure on failure. Add corresponding wait_report/shutdown_report spellings for intentional raw observation. Keep existing wait/shutdown signatures, DriverOutcome and check_shutdown source-compatible, explicitly labelled legacy raw-completion paths in rustdoc with migration links; do not introduce deprecation warnings in this additive stage. Canonical examples and guidance select checked methods. A future breaking rename making bare wait checked is outside this epic. This temporarily preserves conventionally named weaker methods for existing consumers; it is a compatibility concession, not an equivalent recommended path.

D-02 — Retain evidence without requiring another check. ShutdownSuccess is opaque, created only after the existing report classifier accepts the published report. Provide immutable report access and consuming extraction of the same SharedShutdownReport for application policy/diagnostics. No public unchecked constructor, Default, mutable report access or infallible conversion from arbitrary reports. It can be cheaply cloned if useful. Do not require a must_use annotation on the success witness: `wait_checked().await?;` must compile under deny(unused_must_use); the Result already requires handling. Raw reports keep their existing must_use contract. ShutdownFailure retains the complete shared report or original shared JoinError, with current redacted top-level formatting and explicit cause access. Reuse one internal classification path with check_shutdown; do not create a second success predicate.

D-03 — Observe existing completion, do not re-own it. Checked methods borrow self, await the existing publication and classify its frozen evidence. Wait never requests shutdown; shutdown requests it without approving readiness. Cancellation of a checked waiter cannot cancel the coordinator or cleanup, and observation does not extend process ownership. Preserve last-owner drop, repeat/late observers and published report identity. Runtime loss before publication retains the documented panic limitation; do not invent a report or claim cleanup succeeded. Later native settlement must not rewrite a previously unsuccessful report or run skipped finalizers.

D-04 — Application semantics and diagnostics stay local. Reference runtime receives successful evidence directly, preserves its required pool-record check and RuntimePoolCleanupFailure identity, and propagates generic failures as ShutdownFailure. Consumers with body and shutdown outcomes must await and retain both before returning. Do not flatten rich shutdown errors into strings/count-only errors, or erase an independent application error while simplifying completion. Downstream summary logging must still see successful reports and ShutdownFailure::Report before propagation. Match a borrowed checked result (success report accessor / existing Report variant / Coordinator without a report), then propagate that same result; never wait twice, clone merely to classify, or fall back to raw observation solely to print a summary. Keep logging conditional and application-owned. Worker readiness rejection and timeout remain application failures even when shutdown succeeds; if shutdown also fails, retain ShutdownFailure in the existing contextual error chain. Preserve wait-versus-request-shutdown behavior and await completion before returning the readiness failure. Do not change maintenance retry policy, promote ordinary database maintenance errors to fatal exits, or migrate Command/StartupObserver waits.

D-05 — Actual consumer verification has source provenance. T-02 uses disposable copies of the two identified consumer revisions, with original checkouts and pins untouched. Preserve unrelated work. First record and run the focused baseline with its pinned graph; then override all packages sourced from Batter's repository coherently to the exact candidate tree in the copy, including direct native Runledger/Runlimit packages and the existing SQLx patch when present. Inspect Cargo metadata/lock sources, features and dependency paths to prove one compatible identity per shared package; an unused patch, stale Git pin or duplicate old/new type graph invalidates candidate evidence. Cargo generates any trial lock changes; never hand-edit Cargo.lock. Adapt only completion calls and necessary report-summary extraction in the disposable copy. Dependency/toolchain/API failures already present in the baseline or caused by unrelated newer APIs must be isolated and recorded, not repaired by silently broadening this epic. The generic external regressions still run independently of sibling paths. If candidate rehearsal remains blocked, T-01 can finish, but T-02 must not claim both-consumer compatibility or close with that acceptance unmet. Permanent downstream adoption, source-pin updates and repository-wide upgrade policy remain separately scoped.

D-06 — Precise diagnostic boundary. Test checked propagation into both BoxError and anyhow::Result, including downcast to ShutdownFailure and retained causes. Redaction assertions cover Batter wrapper Debug/Display and deliberately selected summary fields. Do not assert that arbitrary anyhow Debug/source-chain rendering or native panic hooks are payload-free; retain the source contract and state this limit in the relevant recipe. This epic does not redesign application logging or install a global hook.

Routine private module layout, accessor spelling and fixture reuse are implementer choices within these contracts. Widening success semantics, dropping evidence, changing legacy signatures or introducing a different ownership protocol requires revising this design before dependent work.

## Execution graph

Two sequential delivery tasks: T-01 `batter-r62w.1` (checked core API and contract evidence), then T-02 `batter-r62w.2` (canonical consumers, downstream-shaped regressions and two isolated compatibility rehearsals). Child Beads contain the task contracts; native blocker edges are authoritative. T-01 has no external blocker. T-02 needs both supplied downstream snapshots and their focused offline build prerequisites; those are named verification inputs, not dependencies on unrelated tracker tasks. Do not parallelize these tasks: they share the public interface and contract documentation. First safe action is to claim T-01 after br show/ready, inspect current driver/report/test code and start its Jig work plan.

## Verification

Every code-changing child follows AGENTS.md: relevant focused tests, `bash scripts/verify.sh`, `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh` (including rustdoc), rebuild the HTTP example and execute all five documented scripts/smoke_http.py profiles, and obtain a final current-input passing api:test receipt through Jig. Inspect work evidence/gates before repeating tests; reuse valid evidence only with matching commands, toolchain, environment and prerequisites. Use Jig work start/check/evidence/gates/finish for substantial implementation. If new fixtures or source roots need scope changes, update .jig.toml and .agent/jig-contract.json together; keep formatting/contract/file-budget gates as profile siblings.

The core oracle is end-to-end propagation through a helper whose only completion statement is checked await plus question-mark, independent failure scenarios, preserved identities and cancellation behavior. A test that only compares checked output to is_success is insufficient. Public external consumer controls must compile the ordinary question-mark recipe with unused_must_use denied through both BoxError and anyhow, import the identical facade/core types, and reject forging the success witness for the intended privacy/trait reason. T-02 additionally executes generic service/worker/diagnostic scenarios and candidate rehearsals at the actual application boundaries; a source audit or unchanged-pin compile does not satisfy those checks. No benchmark framework or fresh-agent evaluation infrastructure is part of this epic; any fresh-agent usability exercise remains explicitly proposed/unexecuted until recorded.

Record commands, toolchain, platform, results, failures/prerequisites and exact evidence in the owning Bead. The focused downstream rehearsals require no new live database: compile static SQL using committed metadata with SQLX_OFFLINE=true and execute non-ignored lifecycle/maintenance tests. Downstream live PostgreSQL/signal suites are supplementary evidence, require their own disposable fixtures, and stay explicitly unexecuted unless actually run; do not turn them into a prerequisite for a local result-classification proof. Existing Batter verification and affected in-repository live requirements remain as stated in the children. For any full shutdown smoke use a directly launched binary or adequate process-manager grace; the shared service development proxy allows only two seconds and cannot prove its full shutdown contract. Current Linux/macOS claims require executed evidence; no hosted CI claim follows from local configuration. Tracker-only planning does not require rerunning Rust suites.

## Rollout and recovery

Land the additive core capability before migrating consumers. Existing compiled-source contracts remain available; no storage migration or new dependency is needed. If consumer migration exposes a regression, contain it by retaining that consumer's old explicit checked flow until repaired, without removing semantic tests or accepting failed reports. If the classifier/ownership contract cannot be preserved, do not claim completion. No commits, publication or deployment are authorized by this planning request.

## Risks and open decisions

description:

### T-01 — Expose checked owned-process completion with retained evidence
- Outcome: all owned lifecycle wait/shutdown entrypoints have a checked result that propagates meaningful shutdown failure through ordinary question-mark, with explicit raw-report alternatives and preserved legacy APIs.
- Context: follow parent epic decisions D-01 through D-03 and diagnostic boundary D-06. Existing driver.rs owns classification, published outcomes and owner/observer forwarding; report.rs owns the success predicate. Do not modify coordinator scheduling to implement a result adapter.
- Changes: crates/batter-core/src/lifecycle/driver.rs and lifecycle.rs exports; report.rs rustdoc; core lifecycle/startup/managed rustdoc examples; tests/driver_observer.rs, tests/process_ownership/report_usage.rs, tests/report_redaction.rs and existing lifecycle/managed failure fixtures as appropriate; relevant guarantees, implemented-status row and changelog. Document the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment in the Bead, including the compatibility exception and locally unenforceable deliberate error disposal.
- Depends on: none
- Verify: focused core integration tests and doctests; successful completion; critical early Ok/error/panic; fatal finite failure; failed/panicked/timed-out/skipped cleanup; abort requests and unjoined work; failed/pending native settlement; empty supervisor; coordinator JoinError. Use actual driven failures wherever practical and controlled reports only for otherwise inaccessible classifier branches. Prove a helper containing only checked await/question-mark returns failure and retains original task plus cleanup causes together. Cover both owner types and observer forwarding, no implicit readiness approval, waiter cancellation while cleanup is blocked, last-owner drop, repeated/late observation and shared pointer/source identity. Preserve cooperative forced-cancellation success where the existing predicate permits it. Top-level Debug/Display redact private markers; explicit error fields remain inspectable. Provide immutable success-report borrowing that lets application summary code match one checked result on both Ok and Err(Report), then propagate the same outcome; Coordinator has no report. Document that native error-source traversal is outside wrapper redaction. Keep ShutdownFailure downcast/source identity unchanged when converted to anyhow by an external consumer; no new dependency on anyhow belongs in the core. Compile controls prove success cannot be forged, ordinary question-mark causes no success-value lint, and raw-report disposal still triggers the exact lint. Run parent epic verification gates for code changes.
- Recovery: additive API permits retaining legacy callers; revert only task-owned edits if needed. Do not relax is_success, existing failure assertions or runtime-loss limits.
- Done when: checked methods and report alternatives are public on all applicable types; success retains immutable evidence with no unchecked creation path; all failures preserve existing payload identity; classification has one owner; cancellation/ownership behavior is unchanged; compatibility and canonical rustdoc are unambiguous; required verification and invalid-state assessment are recorded.

title: T-02: Adopt checked completion and prove downstream compatibility
description:
Canonical plan and shared decisions: `batter-r62w` (read with `br show batter-r62w --json`). Actual consumer evidence and pin rules are in the parent, D-04 through D-06. Scope is Batter delivery plus disposable compatibility rehearsals; this task does not authorize permanent downstream code or pin updates.

### T-02 — Adopt checked completion and prove actual consumer compatibility
- Outcome: canonical Batter examples and two actual downstream completion patterns use the checked boundary without paired generic inspection, preserving application policy, report diagnostics and original causes.
- Context: build on the T-01 API. Both downstreams already call check_shutdown, so measure removed coordination, not a fictitious current false-success bug. Reference required-pool evidence stays local. The process_owned example currently replaces both failures with a generic error; retain them in a small private application aggregate. Do not broaden into finite Command, startup observer, worker scheduling or maintenance policy changes.
- Changes: crates/batter/examples/{worker,http_service,quota_service,process_owned}.rs and affected tests; examples/postgres-lifecycle/src/main.rs and its error/exit tests; examples/reference-service/src/runtime.rs and completion regressions; facade/direct adapter completion rustdocs; scripts/check_facade_features.py and minimal generic external runtime controls using its existing consumer mechanism; relevant usage/guarantees/integrations/testing/status/changelog/README guidance. Keep real application names and private scenario details out of upstream fixtures and docs. Disposable downstream edits follow the parent D-05 procedure and are evidence artifacts, not shipped changes.
- Depends on: T-01
- Verify: scenarios V1-V5 and candidate procedure C1-C4 below, plus parent two-toolchain/Jig/HTTP gates for changed Batter code. Each required scenario has a positive and failure control; record actual test execution rather than compile-only success. Inspect current receipts before rerunning equivalent checks.
- Recovery: preserve original downstream checkouts, pins and unrelated edits; discard only owned trial copies. Retain a consumer's prior explicit checked flow until its migration preserves all outcomes. No global wait replacement, weaker semantic assertions, hand-edited lockfile, new provisioning layer or unrelated API upgrade.
- Done when: canonical owned-lifecycle recipes use checked completion; raw/legacy calls have explicit low-level or compatibility purposes; V1-V5 pass; both current-source candidate rehearsals C1-C4 pass with exact provenance and no hidden stale source; required Batter evidence passes; documentation states wrapper/error-chain limits and distinguishes source audit, generic regression, actual consumer trial and any unexecuted live/usability evidence. If an external prerequisite or unrelated baseline incompatibility prevents a required rehearsal, record the precise blocker and retain this task open rather than waive compatibility acceptance.

## Required consumer scenarios

- V1, ordinary application boundary: a generic service uses only checked await/question-mark at an anyhow error boundary returning unit (and the existing BoxError control), compiles under deny(unused_must_use), and returns Ok for clean stop. A driven cleanup error returns an anyhow error downcastable to ShutdownFailure::Report with the same report and original typed cause; coordinator failure similarly retains its JoinError. Exercise the same production-style Result-to-ExitCode function for zero versus failure status. Existing happy-path HTTP/container smokes are not negative coverage.
- V2, summary before propagation: borrow the checked result, extract successful evidence or the report in ShutdownFailure::Report, emit only redacted summary/count fields once, then propagate that result. Verify both clean and failed reports produce the intended observation, failures still downcast, private cause markers are absent from selected diagnostics, and Coordinator fabricates no summary/report. No second wait and no fallback raw-report check.
- V3, worker readiness policy: cover normal-ready completion, readiness rejected before completion, and readiness deadline followed by requested shutdown. Clean shutdown must not erase the readiness failure/timeout; unsuccessful shutdown preserves both application context and the typed ShutdownFailure. Await finalizers before return, preserve the difference between passive wait and requested shutdown, and retain unsuccessful-report summaries in all applicable branches. Use controlled signals/barriers/paused time, not a real database or copied domain worker.
- V4, actual retained contracts: reference required postgres.pool record is checked on successful evidence and retains RuntimePoolCleanupFailure; failed pool cleanup stays a generic ShutdownFailure. Body-plus-shutdown errors in process_owned remain independently accessible. Late native settlement and skipped cleanup are not converted to success by consumer logic. Preserve maintenance future destruction before resource cleanup and no work after stop in the actual shared-service trial.
- V5, public/compatibility controls: facade and direct core types are identical; success evidence cannot be forged; raw-report discard still fails for the exact intended lint; wrong success construction fails for the intended privacy/trait reason. Keep native cause identity, existing legacy signatures and source-only compatibility recipes. Do not require arbitrary anyhow Debug/source chains or the native panic hook to redact payloads.

## Candidate rehearsal procedure

C1. Find the two user-supplied sibling roots by the source revisions and symbols recorded in the parent. Freeze their actual reviewed snapshots and record dirty state, toolchain, manifest/lock hashes and source pins. Locate the shared serving manifest from `crates/*-process/src/serve.rs::ServeProcess`, the worker-bearing binary from `apps/*-api/src/runtime.rs::WorkerProcess`, and the second runtime from `crates/*-runtime/src/lib.rs` containing the check_shutdown call. Resolve exact package names/targets through Cargo metadata; do not hardcode private names into a committed harness. Read each nearest guide. Establish a focused original-pin baseline in disposable copies; no credentials or dotenv files need to be copied or printed.

C2. In a separate candidate copy override the entire relevant Git source graph to the exact completed Batter tree, preserving feature selection. The first consumer directly selects Runledger and Runlimit from the same Git repository; the second has a matching SQLx patch. A facade-only override is not enough. Let Cargo update the trial lockfile, then run subsequent checks with --locked. Use cargo metadata/tree to prove all candidate-facing Batter/native package identities are the intended ones, without an old core or duplicate shared SQLx identity. Record source replacement and minimal completion migration diff; recheck metadata after edits.

C3. Set SQLX_OFFLINE=true for these focused commands against committed query metadata. In the first trial run `cargo test --locked --manifest-path "$SERVING_MANIFEST" --lib serve::tests::`, check both API binary manifests with `cargo check --locked --manifest-path "$API_MANIFEST" --all-targets`, and run the worker binary's non-ignored tests with `cargo test --locked --manifest-path "$WORKER_MANIFEST" --bin "$WORKER_BIN" runtime::tests::` using its metadata-derived binary name. Adapt the three WorkerProcess branches and its report-summary helper, not its work/cleanup policy. Ensure failure-summary and timeout-combination gaps are covered by V2/V3 even if current downstream tests do not cover them. In the second trial run `cargo test --locked --manifest-path "$SERVICE_RUNTIME_MANIFEST" --lib` both without and with `--features db`, then check both API binary manifests/all targets. Execute maintenance ordering/no-post-stop controls and preserve StartupObserver/Command tests. Record actual pass counts, skipped ignored cases and any baseline versus candidate failure; a zero-selected-test run is not evidence.

C4. Keep the two compatibility trials distinct from deployed adoption and from independent fresh-agent usability evaluation. Existing downstream live suites require their documented disposable PostgreSQL/Docker support and are supplemental here; do not run a two-second development-proxy stop as full drain evidence. For changes to Batter's PostgreSQL/reference consumer completion paths, execute affected existing in-repository lifecycle tests and the documented live acceptance needed for those paths before claiming live integration; name exact selected cases and missing prerequisites in the Bead. No new downstream database provisioning or permanent pin upgrade belongs to this task.

title: Bind at-rest rewrap output to its source envelope
description:
## Outcome
Make metadata-only rotation return the input descriptor already paired with its replacement wrapped key. The canonical caller persists a complete replacement envelope without a second wrapper-attachment call. This removes a local API/availability hazard; it is not a reported confidentiality break or a proof of correct remote persistence.

## Evidence and readiness audit
Audited 2026-09-23 at f5e0074e30558599ff65a54f307c75abafc16a2e. `crates/batter-at-rest/src/crypto.rs::Keyring::rewrap` returns `WrappedKey`; `src/format.rs::Envelope::{with_wrapped_key,from_parts}` can attach it to another descriptor. Authentication rejects that composition only when used. `tests/public_api.rs` currently demonstrates the paired rewrap/attach sequence. Closed batter-mlk improved documentation and failure coverage without changing these signatures. Existing `Envelope` already has private fields, canonical encoding, split-part accessors and redacted Debug, so another result type is unnecessary.

## Design and compatibility decision
- Add the preferred `Keyring::rewrap_envelope(&self, context: &Context, envelope: &Envelope) -> Result<Envelope, Error>`. Internally authenticate/rewrap once and assemble the result with the input descriptor. Accept no destination envelope or caller-supplied replacement descriptor. Do not introduce an implicit conversion from the result to a bare wrapper.
- Use one internal cryptographic implementation for the new method and existing `rewrap`. Preserve the latter's signature and behavior for compatibility. Keep `WrappedKey::decode_for`, `Envelope::from_parts` and `with_wrapped_key` for explicit low-level/split-storage use. Put prominent "Low-level compatibility" or "Low-level reconstruction" sections on those APIs, link to `rewrap_envelope`, and move all preferred rotation examples to the new method. Do not remove APIs or introduce deprecation warnings in this task; a breaking cutover is unnecessary.
- The protected invariant is descriptor/wrapper pairing at return. Extracting a wrapper and recomposing it is an explicitly weaker escape hatch. A returned `Envelope` is not a general authenticated-body marker: decode/from_parts also construct that type. Header/body association in storage, complete-old-envelope or covering-revision CAS, current key-policy fencing, and durable per-derived-key encryption budgets remain storage/application responsibilities. Do not claim types enforce them.
- Rewrap has no body input and must neither read, copy, authenticate nor rewrite the body. Preserve v1 bytes, limits, HKDF inputs, AAD, errors and authentication-before-same-key-shortcut behavior. Same-key success returns a byte-identical complete envelope with no randomness request or wrapper encryption; changed-key success retains the data key and descriptor and creates one wrapper with fresh randomness. Failure leaves the source unchanged.
- No storage adapter, key-policy engine, new format, dependency, package-version change or persisted-data migration. Old and new callers can coexist. Document migration as replacing `rewrap` plus `with_wrapped_key` with one `rewrap_envelope` call; rollback requires no byte conversion.

## Implementation surfaces
Update `src/crypto.rs`, relevant `src/format.rs` rustdoc, `src/crypto/tests.rs`, and `tests/public_api.rs` under `crates/batter-at-rest`. Add a runnable public rustdoc/README rotation example. Reconcile the wrapper-only wording in the crate's `AGENTS.md` and `docs/format-v1.md` while preserving the normative byte tables. Update the implemented row in root `docs/status.md` and relevant `docs/testing.md` evidence when delivered. Check direct and facade consumers; the detached gate copies `tests/public_api.rs` into a separate artifact-only consumer. Do not alter historical ExecPlans.

## Falsifiable acceptance
1. Public consumer rotates and persists the returned envelope directly, with no manual wrapper attachment. Its descriptor and the original body bytes remain exact; a keyring containing only the new key opens that original body, while an old-only keyring reports `KeyUnavailable`. Split descriptor/wrapper/body round-trip remains available through documented reconstruction.
2. Same-key rotation authenticates before returning an exact envelope; wrong context, tampered wrapper/descriptor and missing source key retain their errors. Private deterministic/failing-random seams verify no same-key randomness, fresh changed-key nonce use, and `RandomnessUnavailable` without a replacement on failure. Run these through the implementation used by the new API.
3. Retain the corrupt-body case: metadata-only rotation succeeds, but opening that body fails `AuthenticationFailed`, for both same-key and changed-key rotation. Unread-body integrity must never be inferred from success.
4. A compile-fail example shows the canonical `Envelope` result cannot be passed directly as a `WrappedKey` to another envelope's composer; pair it with a compiling canonical-use example. Deliberately extract/recompose a wrapper from rotation A with a different descriptor B under the same context and prove authentication rejection. This is a scoped type-shape proof, not a claim that public low-level reconstruction or wrong-record persistence is impossible. Record the ADR-010 invalid-state assessment and remaining owner obligations.
5. Preserve fixed-vector and existing failure tests, old-signature compatibility coverage, value-free errors and redacted output. Exercise the new API through direct package and opt-in facade imports.

## Verification and delivery
During implementation use Jig work tracking. Run `cargo test -p batter-at-rest --locked`, `cargo clippy -p batter-at-rest --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `node crates/batter-at-rest/tests/fixtures/generate-envelope-v1.mjs --check`, and `scripts/check-batter-at-rest-portability.sh` (exact Rust 1.94 detached/package/unpacked/external consumer). Complete both `bash scripts/verify.sh` and `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=1.94.0 bash scripts/verify.sh`, rebuilt HTTP smoke profiles from `docs/testing.md#http-process-smoke-test`, and final fresh Jig `api:test` evidence plus required policy gates; reuse eligible receipts rather than repeat passing work. Keep `.jig.toml` and `.agent/jig-contract.json` exhaustive scopes aligned if new inputs require it. Record actual platform/toolchain results here; proposed checks and fresh-agent evaluations are not execution evidence. Keep Cargo.lock Cargo-generated. Publication/commits are outside this task's authorization.

Depends on: none. batter-gsdx changes decoding, not this contract. Either task can ship first; serialize edits/integration of shared format, docs and public-consumer files without inventing a functional dependency.
acceptance_criteria: The additive canonical Keyring::rewrap_envelope returns a complete Envelope assembled with the input descriptor, removes caller-side wrapper attachment, and preserves old signatures as explicitly weaker compatibility paths. It retains exact v1 bytes and same-key behavior, authenticates before the same-key shortcut, never attests to or touches the body, and leaves sources unchanged on failure. Public consumer, cross-descriptor misuse, scoped compile-fail, deterministic randomness, corrupt-body and old-signature compatibility evidence pass. Storage CAS, policy fencing and encryption budgets remain explicitly external. Required two-toolchain, HTTP, detached Rust 1.94 package/consumer and fresh Jig verification is recorded before closure.
close_reason: Implemented and locally verified complete-envelope rewrap contract

title: Seal HTTP assembly and distinguish low-level composition
description:
Replace AssembledHttp::into_router with an opaque request-only in-process client without Router conversion, route/layer mutation, or serving conversion. Move loose HTTP middleware and raw-router registration helpers into an explicit low_level namespace without root aliases. Canonical examples use HttpBoundary. Preserve Runlimit-owned protected assembly and the reference application's deliberate authentication-before-admission composition through justified low-level seams.

Migrate all callers and documentation; preserve probes, fallback admission, generated correlation, one completion event, scoped dispatch, direct-peer metadata and response-construction lifetime limits. Add compile-fail post-assembly mutation/escape checks and positive client examples plus runtime rejection/timeout/probe/fallback observations. Update contracts/status/ADR-010 assessment and migration guidance. Run focused checks, both verify.sh toolchains, HTTP smokes and final Jig evidence. Complete cumulative native review with zero findings before closing.
